**How pride in this world turns into humiliation at the reckoning.**

As for the disbeliever, his punishment will be lessened for him on the Day of Resurrection, but he will never depart the Fire. (Allah does not wrong the faithful even concerning one good action, for he will be rewarded for it by provision in this life and awarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he will be provided provision in this life for his good action, and on the Day of Resurrection, he will not have any good deed.) Allah describes the horrors, hardships and difficulties of the Day of Resurrection, saying, how would it be on that Day when there will be a witness from every nation, meaning the Prophets, just as Allah said;. That is why he is rejected by the prominent leaders and intellectuals of society: they fail to apprehend that a man devoid of any outward splendour could be so important that God might choose him to communicate His message to mankind. But when Doomsday approaches and the divine court is ready to deliver its verdict, they will be bewildered to see that that very ordinary man, whom they had rejected as being of no value, has been given the honour of becoming God’s witness and has been set above the nations. In that court the rejecters will stand in the enclosure of the accused, while that ordinary man rejected by them will occupy the seat of God’s spokesman. It will be such a terrible and hard moment for the defaulters that they will wish that the earth would rend itself asunder and swallow them up. But their repentance and sense of humiliation will not at that point serve any purpose. The whole record of their speech, actions and thoughts will be with God and they will be told that their rejection of truth was not due to ignorance but pride, that they considered themselves superior to the preacher of truth, and that the acceptance of reality, despite its having been laid before them, appeared to them like setting their own greatness at naught.

43.text:
Turning back to the believers after reminding them of the Day of Judgment, the forty-third verse guards the outward and inward purity of the daily prayer and introduces the merciful dispensation of dry ablution with clean earth. "O believers! Do not approach prayer while intoxicated until you are aware of what you say" sets down the early stage in the gradual prohibition of wine before its total ban, forbidding any believer from standing in prayer while his mind is clouded by drink or heavy slumber until he is fully conscious of the words he is uttering before his Lord. "nor in a state of full impurity, unless you merely pass through the mosque, until you have bathed" bars performing prayer or lingering in the mosque while in a state of major ritual impurity following sexual intimacy or seminal discharge until one has washed the entire body in a ritual bath, while allowing a person who needs only to cross through the mosque from door to door or who is travelling on a road to pass. "But if you are ill, on a journey, or have relieved yourselves, or been intimate with your wives and cannot find water, then purify yourselves with clean earth, wiping your faces and hands" grants the enduring concession of tayammum whenever water is unavailable or harmful to use in illness, whether after minor impurity from relieving oneself or major impurity from marital intimacy, by striking clean earth and wiping the face and hands. "And Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving" seals the ruling by showing that making the clean earth a means of purity is a gift from the Pardoning, Forgiving Lord, teaching the community that prayer is not a mechanical repetition of postures and words with a heedless or clouded mind, but a conscious standing before the King of the worlds in both bodily purity and mental presence, and that when water cannot be found or used, the entire earth has been made a pure place of prayer and a means of cleansing for this community out of the boundless mercy of the Pardoning, Forgiving Lord, while the command not to approach the mosque in major impurity except in passing and not to stand in prayer while drowsy or intoxicated preserves the reverence of the house of prayer and the alertness of the heart in every bowing and prostration, showing once again how the sacred law joins outward and inward purity to ease and compassion for the sick and the traveller in every circumstance of life so that no servant is ever cut off from turning to his Merciful Lord in pure and focused prayer, before the forty-fourth verse returns to warning against the schemes of the opponents of faith.

**Not approaching prayer while intoxicated until you know what you say.**

O you who believe draw not near to prayer that is do not perform prayer whilst you are inebriated by a drink this was revealed concerning being drunk during the congregational prayer; until you know what you are saying when you have sobered up; nor whilst you are defiled as a result of sexual penetration or ejaculation junuban ‘defiled’ is in the accusative because it is a circumstantial qualifier and may be used to refer to the singular or plural — unless you are traversing crossing a way a route that is unless you are travelling — until you have washed yourselves in which case you may perform prayer a proviso is made for the traveller because a different stipulation applies to him as will follow. Allah revealed the following about the Companions of Muhammad prior to the prohibition of intoxicants: (O ye who believe!) in Muhammad and the Qur'an (Draw not near unto prayer) in the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ with the Prophet ﷺ (when ye are drunken, till ye know that which ye utter) so that you know what the prayer leader recites during the prayer, (nor when ye are polluted) nor when you are in a state of major ritual impurity, (save when journeying upon the road) except when passing through when you have to, (till ye have bathed) to purify yourselves from major ritual impurity. O you who have faith in Allah and follow His Messenger, do not pray when you are drunk, until you recover from your drunkenness, and can tell what you are saying. Do not approach Salah while you are in a druken state until you know what you are saying, nor while Junub (sexually impure), except while passing through, until you bathe (your entire body), and if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the Gha'it (toilet), or from 'Lāmastum' (touching) women, but you do not find water, then perform Tayammum with clean earth, rubbing your faces and hands. Allah forbade His believing servants from praying while drunk, for one does not know the meaning of what he is saying in that state, and He forbade them from attending the Masjids while sexually impure, except when one is just passing through the Masjid from one door to another. This Ayah sanctifies the position of the prayer, it being too sacred than to be performed in a defecient manner, like in a state of drunkenness, until one becomes aware of what he is saying, or sexually impure, until he bathes (Ghusl), or after answering the call of nature, until he performs ablution. Based on the rule that performing salah in a state of intoxication is forbidden, according to some commentators, it is also not correct to perform salah when one feels so sleepy that one cannot control what one says. Although the verse was initially revealed to prohibit offering sal ah in a state of intoxication, however, some other situations have also been dealt with in which offering salah is not permitted. This verse appears here to underline the initial prohibition of intoxicants or wine, but it also reveals an important reality about prayer. Prayer does not mean the mere repetition of certain words and motions with accuracy; it must also reflect the concentration of the mind. When he is submitting himself to God with his utterances and his body, his mind and intention should also be in submission to Him. Along with his physical obeisance, his consciousness should inhere in his prayer.

**Major ritual impurity, bathing, and passing through the mosque.**

It is said that the purpose of this verse is to prohibit the approach to places of prayer that is mosques the exception being if one were merely passing through and not staying. (This ruling was before alcohol was completely forbidden.) Do not pray when you are in a state of major ritual impurity, and do not enter the mosques when you are in that state, except in passing, until you have washed your body. 1-Stands for Janabah which signifies a ritual impurity caused by sexual intercourse or seminal discharge, in passion or dream, after which it becomes obligatory to take a bath. The first kind is the state of 'major impurity' or janabah' which is caused by sexual intercourse or by ejaculation with sexual desire by whatever means. This state of impurity has been referred to in the above verses by the word ' " which is derived from janabah and has been translated as 'major impurity'. While the Holy Qur'an has prohibited to 'go near salah’ in a state of major impurity the rule has been made subject to one exception which is expressed in the words (i.e. 'save when you are traversing a way'). It, therefore, means that one cannot go near salah in a state of major impurity without having taken a ritual bath (ghusl), however, if he is 'traversing a way' in the sense that he is on journey and does not find water, he can offer salah without taking bath after making tayammum as explained in the next sentence. He says that 'going near salah' means 'entering a mosque' and it is prohibited for a person to enter a mosque in a state of 'major impurity'. The prohibition of entering a mosque in the state of impurity is based on some other sources, and it is not allowed, even for a passer-by, to enter a mosque with intention to go somewhere else.

**Purifying with clean earth in illness, travel, or absence of water.**

(Lo! Allah is Benign) Allah is Generous for the abundance He has given you, (Forgiving) of any shortcoming that may ensue from you. If you have an illness and cannot use water because of it, or if you are travelling, or have answered the call of nature, or have had sexual relations with women, and you cannot find water, then find clean earth, and wipe your faces and hands with it. (Allah's Messenger saw a person sitting away from the people and not praying with them. He asked him, 'O so-and-so! What prevented you from offering the prayer with the people, are not you Muslim' He replied, 'Yes, O Allah's Messenger! I am Junub and there is no water.' The Prophet said, 'Perform Tayammum with clean earth and that will be sufficient for you.') The linguistic meaning of Tayammum is to intend, as Arabs say, "May Allah 'Tayammamaka' (direct at you) His care." 'Clean earth' means dust. (We were given preference over people in three things. Our lines (in prayer) were arranged in rows to resemble the rows of the angels, all of the earth was made a Masjid for us, and its dust was made clean for us when there is no water.) The face and hands are wiped with one strike on the sand in this case, as Imam Ahmad recorded that 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza said that a man came to 'Umar and asked him, "I am Junub, but there is no water." 'Umar said, "Then, do not pray." 'Ammar said, "Do you not remember, O Leader of the Faithful! (I have been given five things which were not given to any (Prophet) before me: Allah made me victorious with fright that covers a month's distance. The earth has been made for me (and for my followers) a place for praying and an object to perform purification with. Therefore let my followers pray wherever the time of a prayer is due - and in another narration - he will have his means of purity and his Masjid. The spoils of war have been made lawful for me and it was not made so for anyone else before me. I have been given the right of intercession (on the Day of Resurrection.) Every Prophet used to be sent to his nation exclusively, but I have been sent to all mankind.) This procedure is called 'Tayammum' and has been taken by the Shari'ah as a symbol of ritual purification where the actual act of purification through water is not possible or is extremely difficult. The words ('i.e. or one of you has come after easing himself) refer to the 'minor impurity' while the words (i.e. 'or you have touched women') stand for having sexual intercourse) causing major impurity. It is certainly a great favour granted by Allah Almighty that He, in His mercy, has made something else to take the place of water, something which is much more easily available than water. It has, therefore, been permitted that, if there is any risk to health, one may perform dry ablution tayammum. Tayammum is a way of maintaining that spirit when the usual ablution is not possible. One is drunk with the wine of the grape, another with the wine of heedlessness, another with love for this world, another with the frivolity of the soul and self-love. When someone is drunk with the soul's arrogance and with pride and self-worship, his work is in peril. For every drop of water that passes over your body, God will create an angel that will obey and worship until the Day of Resurrection, and He will give its reward to you. " Thus the ablution for defilement was made mandatory in all the shariahs of the prophets from the era of Adam until the time of the Master of the World-upon all of them be God's blessings and peace!

If they had said ‘We hear and obey’, instead of ‘We hear and disobey’; ‘Listen’, instead of ‘‘Listen to us, may you not hear!"; and had truly said, ‘Watch over us’, then these would have been better for them than what they said, and more appropriate, being worthy and correct behaviour in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ. (And if only they had said: "We hear and obey", and "Do make us understand," it would have been better for them, and more proper; but Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not except a few.) meaning, their hearts are cast away from the path of righteousness and therefore, no beneficial part of faith enters it. (so little is that which they believe)[2:88] which means they do not have beneficial faith. This last aspect is in a way an exhortation to Muslims that they should be careful in choosing the words they use to say what they have to say, for mincing words is not their style. The present verse addresses them directly and commands them to believe in the final revelation and demonstrate their confirmation. Should they continue ignoring the warning and remain hostile, they should really be concerned with the chilling prospects of what their fate would be as a consequence of their ill choice.

**How hair-splitting and shamelessness kept all but a few from faith.**

The book of God is given to a community so that it may rectify the thinking and conduct of its people. But when the bearers of the Divine Book, like the Jews, suffer from decline, they begin to take misguidance in place of guidance from it. The commands of God become the subject of futile hair-splitting discussions; concocted philosophies are produced in the name of theology, and wrongdoers alter the divine book to justify the religious validity of their actions. They detach the words of God from their context and interpret them on the basis of their own assumptions. The Jews having received a portion of the Book means that they were able to read the words of the Book, but could not mould their actions according to those words, thereby defeating the real purpose of the Scriptures. They remained the bearers of the Book so far as its words were concerned, but in the matter of practice they adopted the ways of other worldly communities. Moreover, while the others practised worldliness in the name of worldliness, the Jews adopted the same worldly ways but had the audacity to try to justify their practices by misquoting the Divine Book. They practiced a deception but did not realize the way in which He deceived them in that they were given the book and then were deprived of the bless ing of understanding so that they distorted [the words] and persisted [in their unbelief]. They acted shamelessly toward the Messenger and refused to show him respect so they were punished with doubt concerning his affair. Those who acted shamelessly devised a barrier between themselves and the blessing of [the Prophet's] companionship and the bounties of serving him. If they had hastened [instead] to reject the envy they felt and had accepted his state with venera tion and honored [him] they would have found blessing in following him and happiness in both abodes. But how could they be otherwise when what had already been determined distanced themḍ They were kept back by fate qisma from the carpet of service khidma.

47.text:
Turning from describing the conduct of the hostile scholars in the third person, the forty-seventh verse addresses the People of the Book directly face to face with a solemn call to faith before the door of respite closes. "O you who were given the Book! (And the commandment of Allah is always executed) after the revelation of this verse 'Abdullah Ibn Salam and his companions embraced Islam. 48.text:
Following the forty-seventh verse's warning to the People of the Book, the forty-eighth verse lays down the supreme dividing line in the court of Allah between the one unforgivable sin if a person dies upon it and all other sins beneath it. "Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him in worship" proclaims as an unalterable rule that anyone who dies ascribing a partner to Allah in His divinity, His attributes, His unseen knowledge, or His exclusive right to worship cuts himself off permanently from forgiveness, because he has given the right of the Creator to a creature. "but forgives anything else of whoever He wills" immediately opens the boundless ocean of divine mercy for every sin short of polytheism and disbelief: whoever meets Allah affirming His Oneness, even if burdened with grave sins, lies within the will and grace of Allah, who either pardons him outright without punishment or purifies him and brings him at last into Paradise, while every sin including shirk itself is forgiven whenever a person repents before death. "And whoever associates others with Allah has indeed committed a grave sin" seals the verse by naming polytheism as the greatest fabrication and most tremendous wrong in existence, so that no believer ever despairs of Allah's mercy over a sin from which he repents, and no one ever imagines that associating created beings with the Creator in worship, unseen knowledge, or sovereign power is a light matter, for the Creator who brought all things into being without partner welcomes back any servant who meets Him free of shirk, even with an earth's fill of shortcomings, making pure monotheism the unshakeable foundation of eternal salvation, forgiveness, and hope in the Hereafter, before the forty-ninth verse exposes the delusion of those who boast of their own spiritual purity.

**Why Allah never forgives dying upon shirk and the forms of associating partners with Him.**

God forgives not that anything should be associated with Him. (Lo! Allah forgiveth not that a partner should be ascribed unto Him) if one dies in such a state. Allah does not forgive that anything from His creation should be associated to Him. And the commandment of Allah is always executed Verily, Allah forgives not that partners should be set up with Him (in worship), but He forgives except that to whom He wills; and whoever sets up partners with Allah in worship, he has indeed invented a tremendous sin. (forgives not that partners should be set up with Him (in worship),) meaning, He does not forgive a servant if he meets Him while he is associating partners with Him,. But, from among those to whom this admonition has been addressed, some could finally be forgiven, which admits of the probability that all these other addressees may, perhaps, be also forgiven. Therefore, the text goes on to explain that this group of people will not be forgiven because of their kufr or disbelief. The words of the Qur'anic text in ‌ ‌ (Surely, Allah does not forgive the ascribing of a partner to Him) demonstrate that the set articles of faith relating to the Being and Attributes of Allah Almighty are the sine qua non of religion and holding any belief similar to these in favour of whoever and whatever He has created is shirk. This is the ascribing of a partner to Allah in matters of knowledge ( ‘ilm), for example believing that a certain pious person or a spiritual master or the head of a mystical order knows about everything in this universe all the time. Other forms could be asking an astrologer or a fortune-teller or a diviner about things that are going to take place in a person's life, things which belong to the unseen world, an exclusive domain of Allah; or, to take omen from the words written by a pious person and believing that it has got to happen; or, calling someone from a considerable distance and believing that the person has become all aware of the call; or, keeping a fast dedicated to someone other than Allah. This is ascribing to others the powers and rights which are the exclusive domain of Allah as for example, taking someone to have the power and authority to provide gain or inflict loss. This means the ascribing of a partner to Allah in acts of worship ( Ibadah) which is the sole due of Allah. Some of the forms it could take are to go down in sajdah (prostration) for anyone, to release an animal dedicated in the name of somebody, making cere-monious offering for a person or thing, living or dead, to make a vow (mannat, nadhr) in someone's name; to make tawaf (rounds, circumambulation) of someone's grave or house; to give preference to someone else's word, or custom, as against God's own command; to make bows before anyone in the manner of a ruku, the bowing position peculiar to Muslim prayer; to slaughter an animal in the name of someone; to take the affairs of the mortal world as subservient to the effect and influence of stars; to regard some month as ill-omened, wretched; and things like that.

**Forgiving every sin short of shirk for whoever Allah wills.**

But He forgives other than save that of sins to whomever He wills forgiveness for by admitting him into Paradise without punishment. And whomever He wills of the believers He punishes for their sins and then admits them into Paradise. He forgiveth save that to whom He will) to whomever repents. This verse was revealed about Wahshiyy, the murderer of Hamzah, the uncle of the Prophet ﷺ. Besides this and disbelief, He pardons the disobedience of whomever He wills, out of His bounty. Or He punishes those He wills among them according to their disobedience, out of His perfect justice. (Allah said, "O My servant! As long as you worship and beg Me, I will forgive you, no matter your shortcomings. O My servant! If you meet Me with the earth's fill of sin, yet you do not associate any partners with Me, I will meet you with its fill of forgiveness.") ("No servant proclaims,'There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah,' and dies on that belief, but will enter Paradise." I said, "Even if he committed adultery and theft?" He said, "Even if he committed adultery and theft." I asked again, "Even if he committed adultery and theft?" He said, "Even if he committed adultery and theft." The fourth time, he said, "Even if Abu Dharr's nose was put in the dust.") (Verily, Allah forgives not that partners should be set up with Him (in worship), but He forgives except that (anything else) to whom He wills;), and his saying,.

**Why setting up a rival to the Creator is a tremendous fabricated sin.**

(Whoso ascribeth partners to Allah, he hath indeed invented a tremendous sin) a tremendous lie. Whoever worships others next to Allah has committed a terrible sin, which is not forgiven if someone dies still doing it. (and whoever sets up partners with Allah in worship, he has indeed invented a tremendous sin.) is similar to His statement,. (Verily, joining others in worship with Allah is a great Zulm (wrong) indeed.)[31:13] In the Two Sahihs, it is recorded that Ibn Mas'ud said, "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah! (To make a rival with Allah, while He Alone created you.)" As this attitude becomes more established, the person becomes irresponsive, as if the features of his face had been obliterated and he is seeing and listening with the back of his head where there are neither eyes nor ears. Such blindness and deafness to the truth and reality indicate that God has deprived that person of His blessings due to his constant negligence of truth and reality. This extreme stage of insensitivity takes the form of ‘maskh’, that is, a metamorphosis from a superior state to an extremely inferior state; man, the most superior form of creature, is degraded to the level of the beasts. Surely God does not forgive that anything be associated with Him, but less than that He forgives for whomsoever He wills. The associationism of the common people is one thing, and the associationism of the elect some thing else. The greater associationism is that they should say that the tremendous Enactor, the eternal Artisan, has an associate and partner, or they should consider Him to have an equal and peer, or they should make Him similar to something of creation. The right belief and pure religion is that you consider the God of the world's folk and Creator of all to be pure of and incomparable with spouse, child, and partner. He is free of new arrival, change, and birth, hallowed beyond defect, incapacity, and need, pure in attribute, fitting in artisanry, sweet in speech, and complete in love. He is pure of fault in attributes, pure of blunder in deeds, pure of negligence in speech, and pure of doubt in love.

49.text:
After the forty-eighth verse demolished the false hope that anyone could be saved without pure monotheism, the forty-ninth verse confronts the boastful claim of those who declared themselves already pure and guaranteed salvation by their lineage and title. "Have you O Prophet not seen those who falsely elevate themselves" points to the Jewish and Christian claimants who praised themselves as free of sin, boasted that they were the children and beloved ones of Allah, and asserted that none would enter Paradise except their own group, a habit of self-praise and spiritual conceit that Islam bars even in the naming of children or the praising of one's own piety. "It is Allah who elevates whoever He wills" answers their boast by restoring judgment to Allah alone, who knows the hidden reality of every heart and purifies through faith and righteous humility whomever He knows to be worthy. "And none will be wronged even by the width of the thread of a date stone" closes the verse with a vivid image from daily life in Arabia, the tiny, weightless fibre running down the cleft of a date pit, assuring every human being that in Allah's court no one's deeds are ever diminished by even that slender thread, teaching every servant that the closer a person draws to Allah the more humble he becomes regarding his own deeds, leaving the verdict of purity entirely to the All-Knowing Lord who never diminishes the slightest grain of righteous effort, while the fiftieth verse marvels at the audacity of inventing such claims in Allah's name.

**Those who praise themselves for purity and why self-sanctification is forbidden.**

Have you not seen those who praise themselves for purity? namely the Jews when they say ‘We are God’s children and His beloved’ in other words it is not a matter of their purifying themselves. (Hast thou not seen) have you not been informed in the Scripture about (those who praise themselves for purity?) those who absolve themselves from transgression. The reference here is to Buhayr Ibn 'Amr and Marhab Ibn Zayd. Do you not know, O Messenger, the affair of those who are full of praise for themselves and of what they do? (Have you not seen those who claim sanctity for themselves?) was revealed about the Jews and Christians when they said, 'We are Allah's children and His loved ones.'" Ibn Zayd also said, "This Ayah was revealed concerning their statement,. (None shall enter Paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian)." [2:111] This is why Allah said,. Let us now turn to the word of Allah in: ‌ (Have you not seen those who claim sanctity for themselves?) Since the Jews claimed sanctity for themselves, Allah Almighty censures them in this verse as a strange lot attributing sanctity to themselves and then having the audacity to tell others that this is so. From here we learn that it is not permissible for anyone to claim and broadcast his or her sanctity, or that of others. As to the end of man, only Allah knows if it will come in a state of Taqwa and Taharah, that is, in a state when one is still God-fearing spiritually and free from major and minor impurities physically. As such, Sayyidah Zaynab daughter of Abi Salamah narrates that the Holy Prophet asked her: 'What is your name?' Since, at that time, her name was Barrah (which means pure from sins), so, that was what she told him. (Do not claim sanctity for yourselves (that is, do not claim purity and freedom from sins) because it is Allah alone who knows best as to who among you is of the righteous. He, then, named her Zaynab (instead of Barrah). (Mazhari) The third reason for this prohibition is that such a claim gives people the false idea that the person making that claim is nearer to Allah because he is free of all faults, although this is a lie, for no mortal man is free of one or the other shortcoming.

**Allah alone purifies whom He wills and wrongs no one by the thread of a date stone.**

Nay God purifies whom He will through faith and they shall not be wronged they shall not be diminished of their deeds a single date-thread as much as the peel on a date-stone. Allah alone praises whomever He wills, because He knows whatever is hidden in people’s hearts, and will not lessen the reward for their actions in any way, not even as much as the thread of a date stone. Nay, but Allah sanctifies whom He wills, and they will not be dealt with injustice even equal to the extent of a 'Fatīl' Look, how they invent a lie against Allah, and enough is that as a manifest sin Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? (Nay, but Allah sanctifies whom He wills,) meaning, the decision in this matter is with Allah Alone, because He has perfect knowledge of the true reality and secrets of all things. (And they will not be dealt with injustice even equal to the extent of a 'Fatīl',) meaning, He does no injustice with anyone's compensation in any part of his reward, even if it was the weight of a 'Fatīl'. " Yes, at the threshold of a generous man, the more abased you make yourself, the more exalted you become. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that 'Ikrimah said, "Huyay bin Akhtab and Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf (two Jewish leaders) came to the people of Makkah, who said to them, 'You (Jews) are people of the Book and knowledge, so judge us and Muhammad.' They said, 'Describe yourselves and describe Muhammad.' They said, 'We keep relation with kith and kin, slaughter camels (for the poor), release the indebted and provide water for the pilgrims. So who is better, we or him?' They said, 'You are more righteous and better guided.' Thereafter, Allah sent down,. The one who invents in this way does not say anything but that ears reject him and hearts are driven away.

51.text:
Having marveled in the fiftieth verse at how those who claimed guaranteed purity invented falsehoods against Allah, the fifty-first verse exposes the shocking depth to which that spiritual corruption sank when their leaders travelled to Makkah after the battles of Badr and Uhud to forge an alliance with the pagan Quraysh against the Prophet. "Have you O Prophet not seen those who were given a portion of the Scriptures yet believe in idols and false gods and reassure the disbelievers that they are better guided than the believers" calls the Messenger and every listener to witness the spectacle of Jewish scholars such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab, men who possessed knowledge of the Torah and its strict command to worship Allah alone, bowing down before the idols of Makkah to seal a military pact with the polytheists, and then telling the idol-worshippers of Quraysh that their pagan custom of serving pilgrims, slaughtering camels, and keeping ancestral traditions while worshipping stone idols was a truer, more upright path than the pure monotheism and revelation brought by Muhammad and followed by his Companions. Because hatred and envy of the final Messenger blinded them to the most basic truth of their own Scripture, they traded monotheism for the flattery of idolaters, showing that when religious scholars value their own social standing and group pride above the word of God, their outward learning cannot save them from stooping to the lowest compromises with falsehood, and that every person who obeys his own whim or flatters the enemies of truth in order to preserve his worldly influence has set up an idol in his own heart; for when learned men who hold the Torah in their hands bow down to the idols of Quraysh and assure idolaters that their polytheism is superior to the pure monotheism and prayer of Muhammad and his followers, they expose how hatred and fear of losing worldly prestige can corrupt the mind until it calls light darkness and darkness light, trading away the covenant of the prophets for a temporary military alliance with pagans whose cause was already doomed to defeat, and leaving behind a lasting, unmistakable warning for every generation and every religious community against every form of intellectual dishonesty that flatters worldly power at the expense of clear divine truth, a betrayal that the fifty-second verse immediately answers with the curse of Allah.

**The delegation of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf to Makkah and bowing to idols.**

The following was revealed regarding Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf and other such scholars from among the Jews when they came to Makkah and saw those killed at Badr and began to incite the idolaters to avenge them their dead by waging war against the Prophet s Have you not seen those who were given a share of the Book how they believe in al-Jibt and al-Tāghūt two idols belonging to Quraysh and say to the disbelievers to Abū Sufyān and his companions when they the latter said to them ‘Are we who are the guardians of the House who give drink to the pilgrim offer hospitality to the guest set free the captive and do such and such … not more rightly guided than Muhammad he who has contravened the religion of his forefathers severed the ties of kinship and abandoned the Sanctuary? ’ ‘These in other words you are more rightly guided upon a more upright way than the believers’? (Hast thou not seen) have you not been informed, O Muhammad, about (those unto whom a portion of the Scripture has been given) those who have been given knowledge of the Torah in relation to your trait and attribute, the verse of stoning [married people who commit fornication], and similar other issue, namely. Malik Ibn al-Sayf and his friends who were about seventy people, (how they believe in idols) this is Huyayy Ibn Akhtab (and false deities) Ka'b Ibn Ashraf, (and bow they say of those (idolaters) who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah: Sayyidna Ibn Abbas narrates that two chiefs of the Jews, Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Ashraf came along with a group of theirs, after the battle of Uhud, to meet the Quraysh at Makkah. The people of Makkah told Ka'b ibn Ashraf that they were a people who cheated by making false promises. Then, they challenged them to prostrate before two particular idols (Jibt and Taghut) there, if they really meant what they had said. After that, Ka'b told the Quraysh: 'Let thirty people from among you and thirty people from among us come forward so that we declare our resolve before the Lord of the Ka'bah that all of us will jointly fight against Muhammad . As we already know, the Quraysh put forth the condition that he should prostrate before their idols. Here, we see that he squarely stooped to fulfill the condition imposed by the Quraysh, something, contrary to his religion, but he made no effort to stand by his religious beliefs and did not show the courage to part ways with them on so crucial an issue. After the Battle of Uhud, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went to Makkah, accompanied by seventy riders, in order to ally themselves with Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and break the covenant which they had with Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace. Ka'b was the guest of Abu Sufyan while the other Jews were accommodated in the houses of Quraysh. The people of Makkah said: 'Your are people of Scripture and Muhammad has a Scripture and we are not completely sure that this is a scheme that you devised. So if you want us to go along with you, you have to prostrate to these two idols and believe in them', hence Allah's saying (they believe in idols and false deities). Ka'b then said to the people of Makkah: 'Let there be thirty of us and thirty of you; we shall all go to the Ka'bah and cling to it and promise the Lord of the House that we will do our best to fight Muhammad'.

**What Jibt and Taghut mean and flattering the idolaters over the believers.**

Do you not know, O Messenger, and wonder at the state of the Jews – who Allah gave a portion of knowledge – that believe in all sorts of false gods, and flatter the idolaters, saying that they are more rightly guided than the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ. They believe in Jibt and Taghut and say to those who disbelieve, "These people are better guided on the way, " than the believers They are those whom Allah has cursed, and he whom Allah curses, you will not find for him helper. (and say to those who disbelieve, "These people are better guided on the way," than the believers.) preferring the disbelievers over Muslims, because of their ignorance, un-religious nature and disbelief in Allah's Book which is before them. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that 'Ikrimah said, "Huyay bin Akhtab and Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf (two Jewish leaders) came to the people of Makkah, who said to them, 'You (Jews) are people of the Book and knowledge, so judge us and Muhammad.' They said, 'Describe yourselves and describe Muhammad.' They said, 'We keep relation with kith and kin, slaughter camels (for the poor), release the indebted and provide water for the pilgrims. So who is better, we or him?' They said, 'You are more righteous and better guided.' Thereafter, Allah sent down,. They uttered this statement [in Ayah 4:51] to lure the disbelievers into supporting them, and they ultimately gathered their forces for the battle of Al-Ahzab, forcing the Prophet and his Companions to dig a defensive tunnel around Al-Madīnah. Commentators have explained have said that 'Jibt' comes from the Ethiopian language and refers to a magician while 'Taghut' signifies a soothsayer. Sayyidna Umar says that 'Jibt' means magic and 'Taghut' means Satan. Sayyidna Malik ibn Anas is reported to have said that everything worshipped other than Allah is covered by the name 'Taghut'. They all can be implied in one or the other sense, as Jibt was essentially the name of an idol after all, but it was later on that it came to be applied to other things and beings worshipped other than Allah. Contrary to this, Muhammad has abandoned his ancestral religion and he has cut himself off from his own people and, on top of that, he has challenged our ancestral religion by introducing a new religion of his own.'. When Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b al-Ashraf went to the people of Makkah they were asked: 'You are people of Scripture and ancient knowledge, so tell us about us and Muhammad?' 'What do you have to do with Muhammad?' he said. They said: 'We slaughter high-humped camels, give milk on top of water for others to drink, we assist those who are wronged, we do not severe ties of kinship and give water to the pilgrims and our religion is ancient while Muhammad's religion is new'. The Jews said: 'Rather, you are better than him and more guided in your way'. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Hast thou not seen those unto whom a portion of the Scripture hath been given, how they believe in idols and false deities) up to His words, exalted is He, ( and he whom Allah hath cursed, thou (O Muhammad) wilt find for him no helper) [4:52] .

**How following whims and envy expels a person from the service of God.**

It says: 175 (Recite to them the news of the one who was given Our signs, then he eased out from it and followed the Satan, and he was one of those who seduce people to err.) (7:175) But, when he launched his sinister plans against Sayyidna Musa in an effort to achieve his personal desires, he was unable to achieve anything against him, but what did happen was that he himself ended up being accursed and went astray. Hence, when non-Jewish Arabs started supporting the Prophet, the Jews became his opponents to save the facade of their religiousness. In this way their being misguided did not remain confined to themselves and they began to raise controversies about the life and teachings of the Prophet. This was to confuse people and to prove that he was not the Messenger of God but a self-proclaimed proponent of religion working towards fulfilling his ambition of becoming a leader. As this attitude becomes more established, the person becomes irresponsive, as if the features of his face had been obliterated and he is seeing and listening with the back of his head where there are neither eyes nor ears. Such blindness and deafness to the truth and reality indicate that God has deprived that person of His blessings due to his constant negligence of truth and reality. This extreme stage of insensitivity takes the form of ‘maskh’, that is, a metamorphosis from a superior state to an extremely inferior state; man, the most superior form of creature, is degraded to the level of the beasts. Have you not seen those who were given a share of the Book how they believe in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt and say to the disbelievers These are more rightly guided than the believers ḍ Those are the ones whom God has cursed; and he whom God has cursed you will never find for him any helper. The Ṭāghūt of each person is his lower self and his whim-the idol he seeks among that which is other than [God]. When someone pays heed to a person or looks to a reason or turns to a cause or obeys a whim that thing is his jibt and his Ṭāghūt.61 The companions of al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt deserve the curse which is being expelled from the carpet of service ʿubūdiyya and veiled from witnessing lordship rubūbiyya.

52.text:
Answering the betrayal described in the fifty-first verse, where scholars of the Book bowed to idols and pronounced pagan polytheists better guided than the believers, the fifty-second verse delivers Allah's verdict upon them and upon all the worldly alliances they hoped would save them. "It is they who have been condemned by Allah" names those who knowingly championed idolatry against the Messenger of Allah as the very people cast far away from divine mercy, stripped of the spiritual light they once claimed to represent, and left in the disgrace and insensibility of the accursed, while the prophetic teachings under this verse also warn believers against every deed that draws down Allah's curse and against flinging curses lightly at others. "And whoever is condemned by Allah will have no helper" exposes the futility of the pact they went to Makkah to sign: because they sought strength and protection from the idolaters by betraying the truth of Allah, neither the armies of Quraysh nor the confederates they later gathered at the Trench could avail them in this world or shield them from the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, for when the Almighty casts a people out of His mercy no creature in the heavens or the earth can come to their aid, for being accursed in the sight of Allah means being deprived of the grace to recognize truth and left in spiritual blindness where neither ancestral lineage nor military pacts with polytheists can bring victory in this life or deliverance on the Day of Judgment, because the curse of Allah is not an empty word but a real removal of divine protection and guidance that caused their plots at Medina and Khaybar to collapse in humiliation and will leave them on the Last Day without friend, intercessor, or defender, since no creature in the heavens or on the earth can reverse the decree of Allah once a people have knowingly chosen falsehood over His clear revelation, before the fifty-third verse asks whether they imagine they hold a share in Allah's dominion.

**Cast far from the mercy of Allah for allying with idolatry against the truth.**

Those are the ones whom God has cursed; and he whom God has cursed you will never find for him any helper anyone to protect him from His chastisement. (Those are they whom Allah hath cursed) Allah has punished them by imposing on them the capitation tax, (and he whom Allah hath cursed) he whom Allah punishes in this world or in the Hereafter, (thou) O Muhammad (wilt find for him no helper) to save him from Allah's punishment. Those who have these corrupt beliefs are removed from Allah’s mercy, and whoever is removed from Allah’s mercy you will find no helper to protect them. They believe in Jibt and Taghut and say to those who disbelieve, "These people are better guided on the way, " than the believers They are those whom Allah has cursed, and he whom Allah curses, you will not find for him helper. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that 'Ikrimah said, "Huyay bin Akhtab and Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf (two Jewish leaders) came to the people of Makkah, who said to them, 'You (Jews) are people of the Book and knowledge, so judge us and Muhammad.' They said, 'Describe yourselves and describe Muhammad.' They said, 'We keep relation with kith and kin, slaughter camels (for the poor), release the indebted and provide water for the pilgrims. This Ayah [4:52] contains a curse for the Jews and informs them that they have no supporter in this life or the Hereafter, because they sought the help of the idolators. They uttered this statement [in Ayah 4:51] to lure the disbelievers into supporting them, and they ultimately gathered their forces for the battle of Al-Ahzab, forcing the Prophet and his Companions to dig a defensive tunnel around Al-Madīnah. (And Allah drove back those who disbelieved in their rage, they gained no advantage (booty). Allah sufficed for the believers in the fighting. And Allah is Ever All-Strong, All-Mighty). [33:25]. The Qur'anic word, 'la'nah' (translated as 'curse' in absence of a more exact equivalent) means being far removed from the mercy of Allah, extremely debased and disgraced. The words of the Holy Qur'an in verse 52: ‌ state that anyone under the curse of Allah has no helper to help him in that predicament. When Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b al-Ashraf went to the people of Makkah they were asked: 'You are people of Scripture and ancient knowledge, so tell us about us and Muhammad?' 'What do you have to do with Muhammad?' he said. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Hast thou not seen those unto whom a portion of the Scripture hath been given, how they believe in idols and false deities) up to His words, exalted is He, ( and he whom Allah hath cursed, thou (O Muhammad) wilt find for him no helper) [4:52] . After the Battle of Uhud, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went to Makkah, accompanied by seventy riders, in order to ally themselves with Quraysh against the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, and break the covenant which they had with Allah's Messenger, Allah bless him and give him peace. So if you want us to go along with you, you have to prostrate to these two idols and believe in them', hence Allah's saying (they believe in idols and false deities). Ka'b then said to the people of Makkah: 'Let there be thirty of us and thirty of you; we shall all go to the Ka'bah and cling to it and promise the Lord of the House that we will do our best to fight Muhammad'.

**The meaning of Allah's curse in the sacred law and warnings against invoking it.**

In still another hadith, the Holy Prophet has said: 'There are six types of people I have cursed and Allah Almighty has also cursed them - and every prophet is blessed with the acceptance of his prayers - those six are: and one who rises to power by force and terror, then honours a person disgraced by Allah and brings disgrace on a person honoured by Allah;. one who takes as lawful what has been made unlawful by Allah;. the person in my progeny who rules what has been forbidden as lawful;. In another hadith, he said: 'Allah curses the ogler and the ogled at.' It means that the curse of Allah falls on anyone who looks at someone in an evil way, someone who is a non-Mahram, that is, someone outside the count of those in the family he is permitted to see because marriage with them is forbidden forever. The curse of Allah be on the tattooers and the tattooed, on the pickers of eye-brows and the cleavers of teeth as aids to beauty - they are the makers of alteration in the creation of Allah." Because of the amount of evil it releases, corresponding heavy restrictions have been placed against its use. Invoking La'nah against a Muslim is harm (forbidden) and the sole condition when this can be done against a kafir (disbeliever) is that the imprecator must be sure that the disbeliever will die clinging to his disbelief. "It has been reported by Sayyidna Ibn Abbas that the wind swooped away the sheet-cloak of a man and he cursed the wind, whereupon the Holy Prophet said: 'Do not curse it for it is under orders (from Allah) and (remember) whosoever curses something which does not deserve the curse, then, the curse returns to none but him. In the terminology of the Shari’ ah, when applied to disbelievers, it refers to their being far far off from the mercy of Allah; and when it is applied to Muslims, it refers to their having fallen down the level of the righteous (reported by Shami from a1-Quhistani, v.2, p.836).

**How insensibility to truth leaves the accursed without a helper.**

Hence, when non-Jewish Arabs started supporting the Prophet, the Jews became his opponents to save the facade of their religiousness. In this way their being misguided did not remain confined to themselves and they began to raise controversies about the life and teachings of the Prophet. This was to confuse people and to prove that he was not the Messenger of God but a self-proclaimed proponent of religion working towards fulfilling his ambition of becoming a leader. He will surely side with the faithful and make them successful against misguided opponents. Accursedness is, in fact, the extreme form of man’s insensibility. When he becomes too insensitive to distinguish between right and wrong, this has been called the state of being accursed. As this attitude becomes more established, the person becomes irresponsive, as if the features of his face had been obliterated and he is seeing and listening with the back of his head where there are neither eyes nor ears. Such blindness and deafness to the truth and reality indicate that God has deprived that person of His blessings due to his constant negligence of truth and reality. This extreme stage of insensitivity takes the form of ‘maskh’, that is, a metamorphosis from a superior state to an extremely inferior state; man, the most superior form of creature, is degraded to the level of the beasts. Have you not seen those who were given a share of the Book how they believe in al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt and say to the disbelievers These are more rightly guided than the believers ḍ Those are the ones whom God has cursed; and he whom God has cursed you will never find for him any helper. The Ṭāghūt of each person is his lower self and his whim-the idol he seeks among that which is other than [God]. When someone pays heed to a person or looks to a reason or turns to a cause or obeys a whim that thing is his jibt and his Ṭāghūt.61 The companions of al-Jibt and al-Ṭāghūt deserve the curse which is being expelled from the carpet of service ʿubūdiyya and veiled from witnessing lordship rubūbiyya.

53.text:
Turning from the political failure of their alliance in the fifty-second verse to the inner delusion that drove them to oppose the Messenger, the fifty-third verse exposes both their powerlessness in Allah's kingdom and their extreme stinginess of heart. "Do they have control over shares of the kingdom? If so" rebukes their pretension to sit as judges over who deserves prophethood, revelation, and leadership, reminding them and every listener that sovereignty over this world and the distribution of divine offices belong to Allah alone, and that they possess no share whatsoever in the dominion; and "they would not have given anyone so much as the speck on a date stone" reveals why human beings of such narrow, envious disposition are never entrusted with the keys of Allah's mercy: if they actually held any share of kingdom or authority in their hands, their miserliness is so complete that they would withhold every drop of good from humanity, and above all from Muhammad and his Companions, refusing to part with even the tiny groove or dimple on the back of a date pit, just as another verse observes that if people possessed the treasures of their Lord's mercy they would hold back for fear of spending, proving that divine grace is never locked inside a racial monopoly or handed over to the custody of misers who begrudge the rest of humanity the mercy of God, before the fifty-fourth verse names the true disease behind their hostility, namely envy of Allah's bounty.

**Having no share in the dominion and the rebuke of their claim to privilege.**

Or have they a share in the Kingdom? that is to say they have no share in it whatever and even if they did then they would not give the people a single date-spot that is not even something as worthless as the tiny spot on the back of a date-pit because of the extent of their niggardliness. (Or have they even a share) if the Jews had a share (in the Sovereignty? Then in that case, they would not give mankind) they would not give Muhammad and his Companions (even the speck on a date stone). They do not have any share in the dominion, and if they did, they would not give people anything from it, not even as much as the speck on the surface of a date stone. Then in that case they would not give mankind even a Naqir Or do they envy men for what Allah has given them of His bounty? Allah asked the Jews if they have a share in the dominion. That is merely a statement of rebuke, since they do not have any share in the dominion. Linked with previous verses, the description of Jewish traits of character continues in the present verses as well. The Jews, thinking that they belonged to the race of prophets, projected their community as a sacred one. In consequence, they laid claim to honour and privilege which they justified by the invention of numerous stories and parables. By their own lights, everyone who was Jewish by faith was destined for deliverance and would not be consigned to the fire of Hell. The Quranic statement that ‘it is indeed God who purifies whoever He pleases’ rejects such notion that ‘those who consider themselves pure’ are actually and necessarily so. It clarifies that no one may have honour and privilege on the basis of his links with a race or community; these things depend on the divine law of justice. One who, adhering to the divine law, proves himself deserving of honour, will have honour confered upon him, but one who, by his actions, fails to do so, will never be honoured—no matter which race or community he belongs to. The belief in community-based salvation, whether created by the Jews or any other group, is totally without foundation. To invent such a belief and associate it with God is an attempt to associate falsehood with Him. God does not discriminate between people on the basis of group, community or race.

**Withholding even the speck on the back of a date stone out of stinginess.**

(Then in that case they would not give mankind even a Naqir.) Meaning, if they had a share in the sovereignty and dominion, they would not give anyone anything, especially Muhammad , even if it was the speck on the back of a date-stone, which is the meaning of Naqir according to Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of the scholars. (Say: "If you possessed the treasure of the mercy of my Lord, then you would surely withold it out of fear of spending it.)[17:100] meaning, for fear that what you have might end, although there is no such possibility here. (And man is ever Qatur) meaning Bakhil (stingy). [17:100] Allah then said,. (Or do they envy men for what Allah has given them of His Bounty?) referring to their envy of the Prophet for the great prophethood that Allah entrusted him with. Their envy made them reject him, because he was an Arab and not from the Children of Israel. (Or do they envy men) means, "We are the worthy people, rather than the rest of the people. (Then, We have already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and Al-Hikmah, and conferred upon them a great kingdom.) meaning, We gave the prophethood to the tribes of the Children of Israel, who are among the offspring of Ibrahim and sent down the Books to them. They disputed with their own Prophets; so what about you, O Muhammad , especially since you are not from the Children of Israel? (and of them were (some) who rejected [him].)" Therefore, O Muhammad, the rejection of you because of their disbelief is even more severe and they are even further from the truth that you brought them.

**How avarice and jealousy reject the choice of the Real.**

When decadence sets in among the People of the Book, its adherents begin to live a life of wishful thinking instead of following the commands of God. What can be achieved only through the performance of good deeds, they attempt to gain through sorcery, false beliefs and communion with evil spirits. They continue to pay lip service to religion, but in practice, they follow the path of Satan. Or have they a share in the kingdomḍ then they would not give the people a single date spot naqīr. Or are they jealous of people for the bounty that God has bestowed upon them. For We gave the House of Abraham the Book and wisdom and We gave them a mighty kingdom. When those prone to avarice receive abundance it only increases their distress at the comfort others receive. It is as if such a person drinks water sparingly drop by drop yet gulps down and even drains the very water of his life. Indeed out of jealousy they reject the choice of the Real [who has chosen] whom He will for His friends and they do notapproach them withreverence. The way sunna of God with His friends entails [His] elevation and protection of their honor. The custom of disbelievers is to question and doubt the [divine] power of deliberation so there are some who believe and accept [the friends of God] and some who reject and deny. The mighty kingdom mulk is true knowledge maʿrifa of the King.

54.text:
Following the fifty-third verse's exposure of their stinginess, the fifty-fourth verse names the burning jealousy that made them resent the final Messenger and answers their objections from their own sacred history. "Or do they envy the people for Allah’s bounties? Indeed" asks why they begrudge Muhammad and his Companions the gifts that Allah in His grace has bestowed upon them, whether the supreme gift of final prophethood and revelation given to a descendant of Ishmael rather than the Children of Israel, or the worldly establishment and plural marriages of the Prophet that they carped at while forgetting that envy consumes good deeds as fire consumes wood; and "We have given the descendants of Abraham the Book and wisdom, along with great authority" demolishes both pretexts for their jealousy at once: Muhammad himself comes from the noble house of Abraham, the very tree in which Allah had already placed scripture, prophetic wisdom, and vast royal dominion under prophets such as Moses, David, and Solomon, who combined prophethood with kingship and many wives, so neither the appearance of a prophet from Abraham's line nor the joining of spiritual wisdom with worldly authority and marriage was anything strange to the revelation they already knew, making clear that wishing for another person's spiritual or worldly blessing to disappear is a direct rebellion against the wisdom of the Giver who chooses His messengers on the basis of pure hearts and inner piety rather than group claims, and who already gave the house of Abraham revelation, wisdom, and great kingdom without ever asking the permission of the envious, before the fifty-fifth verse contrasts how people responded to that gift.

**Envying the Prophet and his Companions for the bounty of prophethood and marriage.**

Or nay are they jealous of people namely of the Prophet s for the bounty that God has bestowed upon them in the way of prophethood and abundance of women? In other words they wish that he be deprived of such things saying ‘If he were truly a prophet he would not be concerned with women’. (Or are they jealous) nay, they are jealous (of mankind) of Muhammad and his Companions (because of that which Allah of His bounty hath bestowed upon them?) the Scripture, prophethood and marrying many wives. Rather, they envy Muhammad ﷺ and his Companions because of the prophethood, faith and establishment in the land which Allah has given to them. Then in that case they would not give mankind even a Naqir Or do they envy men for what Allah has given them of His bounty? (Then in that case they would not give mankind even a Naqir.) Meaning, if they had a share in the sovereignty and dominion, they would not give anyone anything, especially Muhammad , even if it was the speck on the back of a date-stone, which is the meaning of Naqir according to Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of the scholars. (Or do they envy men for what Allah has given them of His Bounty?) referring to their envy of the Prophet for the great prophethood that Allah entrusted him with. Their envy made them reject him, because he was an Arab and not from the Children of Israel. (Or do they envy men) means, "We are the worthy people, rather than the rest of the people. The knowledge, the grace, the high rank and the grandeur of mission given by Allah Almighty to the Noble Prophet made Jews all too jealous. Verses 53 and 54 strongly admonish this attitude of theirs, giving two reasons why their envy was unreasonable. The drift of the argument is: 'What is the basis of your envy? If this is because you think you are the real inheritors of the kingdom and what he has been blessed with is actually yours, obviously then, this is all wrong. If your envy is based on the realization that the kingdom, no doubt, did not pass from you onto him, still, the question remains, why did it have to go to him at all.

**Giving the house of Abraham the Book, wisdom, and a mighty kingdom.**

For We gave the House of Abraham his forefather the likes of Moses David and Solomon the Book and wisdom and prophethood and We gave them a mighty kingdom David had ninety–nine women and Solomon had a thousand free women and slavegirls. (For We bestowed upon the house of Abraham) David and Solomon ((of old) the Scripture and Wisdom) knowledge, understanding and prophethood, (and We bestowed on them a mighty kingdom) We honoured them with prophethood and Islam and bestowed upon them sovereignty over the Children of Israel. David had 100 legitimate wives, and Solomon had 300 legitimate wives plus 700 concubines. Why do they envy them when Allah gave the descendants of Abraham the revealed scripture and other revelation besides the scripture, and Allah gave them far-reaching power over people. Then, We have already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and Al-Hikmah, and conferred upon them a great kingdom Of them were (some) who believed in it, and of them were (some) who rejected it; and enough is Hell for burning (them) (Then, We have already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and Al-Hikmah, and conferred upon them a great kingdom.) meaning, We gave the prophethood to the tribes of the Children of Israel, who are among the offspring of Ibrahim and sent down the Books to them. (and of them were (some) who rejected it) by disbelieving in it, ignoring it, and hindering the people from its path, although this bounty was from and for them, the Children of Israel. They disputed with their own Prophets; so what about you, O Muhammad , especially since you are not from the Children of Israel? He too comes from the family of prophets who have ruled over kingdoms before him.

**Why envy is forbidden in both worldly and spiritual excellence.**

It means that Hasad (envy) is a desire to see the other person's blessing somehow disappear, and this is harm (forbidden). "Do not hate and do not envy and do not turn your backs on each other. "Beware of envy, for envy eats up good deeds as the fire eats up wood. "Stealthily creeping into you is the disease of earlier peoples - envy; and hatred, which is a shaver. Envy, whether it be on account of someone's worldly, or spiritual excellence, is harem (forbidden) on both counts, as the words (Is it that they have a share in the kingdom?) seem to point out towards worldly excellence, while the words (the Book and the wisdom) are indicative of spiritual excellence. In real life, the hypocrites tread the path of selfish desires and give in to satanic inducements, but outwardly, bearing the label of religion, they think that their actions are truly guided by God’s religion. In such an atmosphere, whenever the pure Truth is presented to them, they become its bitterest opponents. But the preacher of truth cannot expect any leniency from them, for they become infuriated with jealousy over someone else having been granted religious representation, when they alone had formerly had a monopoly of religion. They quite forget that God chooses the representatives of His religion on the basis of purity of soul, inner piety and a sound heart, and not because of any outward show of piety. Just as starvation and thirst wreck one’s physical existence, similarly deprivation of God’s grace and succour wrecks one’s spiritual existence. It has been said, "The tremendous kingdom is having an overview of the secrets of the creatures," or it is "gazing upon the secrets of the empire such that nothing is hidden. " This is why Abū ʿUthmān Maghribī said, "When someone responds to the Real, the empire re sponds to him. Shaykh al-Islām Anṣārī said, "Servanthood cannot bear more than knowing some and not knowing some, for God says, 'He does not show His unseen to anyone except someone He ap proves as a messenger' [72:26-27]. 'And God will not inform you of the unseen' [3:179]. " It has also been said that the tremendous kingdom is recognition of the tremendous King.

55.text:
Continuing directly from the reminder of the Book, wisdom, and authority granted to the house of Abraham in the fifty-fourth verse, the fifty-fifth verse shows how human beings divided into two camps before that divine blessing and before the final Messenger who came in its line. "Yet some believed in him while others turned away from him" describes the two paths taken by the People of the Book and by humanity at large: a sincere group believed in the revelation given to the descendants of Abraham and consequently recognized and followed Muhammad when he came confirming their Scriptures, while another faction stubbornly rejected him, turned their own faces away from the truth, and actively hindered other people from entering the path of faith out of envy for their lost monopoly on religious leadership. "Hell is sufficient as a torment" closes the warning with austere brevity: for those who not only spurned the gift of guidance themselves but stood in the road to bar others from Allah's Messenger, the roaring blaze of Hell is a complete and sufficient requital for their rebellion, reminding every community that possessing revealed books in the past profits nothing when its people reject and actively obstruct the living truth that Allah sends to confirm their own scriptures, while the fifty-sixth verse immediately unfolds the nature of that punishment in the Fire.

**Dividing into those who believed in him and those who turned away and hindered others.**

And there are some of them who believe in him in Muhammad and some of them who bar from him who reject him and do not believe. (And of them) of the Jews (were (some) who believed therein) believed in the Scripture of David and Solomon (and of them were (some) who disbelieved therein. Hell is sufficient for (their) burning) i.e. Some of the People of the Scripture have faith in what Allah revealed to Abraham ﷺ, and to the prophets among his descendants; and there are those who denied this, and turned people away from having faith in it, and who do the same with what was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Then, We have already given the family of Ibrahim the Book and Al-Hikmah, and conferred upon them a great kingdom Of them were (some) who believed in it, and of them were (some) who rejected it; and enough is Hell for burning (them) (Of them were (some) who believed in it;) referring to Allah's favor and bounty (Prophets, Books, kingship),. (and of them were (some) who rejected it) by disbelieving in it, ignoring it, and hindering the people from its path, although this bounty was from and for them, the Children of Israel. They disputed with their own Prophets; so what about you, O Muhammad , especially since you are not from the Children of Israel? (Of them were (some) who believed in [him],) "Muhammad ,. (and of them were (some) who rejected [him].)" Therefore, O Muhammad, the rejection of you because of their disbelief is even more severe and they are even further from the truth that you brought them.

**How jealousy over religious status drives opponents to reject the truth.**

The knowledge, the grace, the high rank and the grandeur of mission given by Allah Almighty to the Noble Prophet made Jews all too jealous. Verses 53 and 54 strongly admonish this attitude of theirs, giving two reasons why their envy was unreasonable. If this is because you think you are the real inheritors of the kingdom and what he has been blessed with is actually yours, obviously then, this is all wrong. If your envy is based on the realization that the kingdom, no doubt, did not pass from you onto him, still, the question remains, why did it have to go to him at all. It means that Hasad (envy) is a desire to see the other person's blessing somehow disappear, and this is harm (forbidden). Envy, whether it be on account of someone's worldly, or spiritual excellence, is harem (forbidden) on both counts, as the words (Is it that they have a share in the kingdom?) seem to point out towards worldly excellence, while the words (the Book and the wisdom) are indicative of spiritual excellence. In real life, the hypocrites tread the path of selfish desires and give in to satanic inducements, but outwardly, bearing the label of religion, they think that their actions are truly guided by God’s religion. In such an atmosphere, whenever the pure Truth is presented to them, they become its bitterest opponents. On the other hand, the existence of non-believers around them poses no such challenge and, therefore, their attitude towards them remains lax. But the preacher of truth cannot expect any leniency from them, for they become infuriated with jealousy over someone else having been granted religious representation, when they alone had formerly had a monopoly of religion. They quite forget that God chooses the representatives of His religion on the basis of purity of soul, inner piety and a sound heart, and not because of any outward show of piety.

**Why the Fire of Hell is a just punishment for disbelief and envy.**

Hell suffices for a blaze as a chastisement for those who do not believe. The fire of Hell is sufficient as a punishment for those of them who disbelieve. (Then in that case they would not give mankind even a Naqir.) Meaning, if they had a share in the sovereignty and dominion, they would not give anyone anything, especially Muhammad , even if it was the speck on the back of a date-stone, which is the meaning of Naqir according to Ibn 'Abbas and the majority of the scholars. (Say: "If you possessed the treasure of the mercy of my Lord, then you would surely withold it out of fear of spending it.)[17:100] meaning, for fear that what you have might end, although there is no such possibility here. (Or do they envy men for what Allah has given them of His Bounty?) referring to their envy of the Prophet for the great prophethood that Allah entrusted him with. (and enough is Hell for burning (them).), meaning, the Fire is a just punishment for them because of their disbelief, rebellion and defiance of Allah's Books and Messengers. Being accursed is to be deprived of the grace and succour of God. Just as starvation and thirst wreck one’s physical existence, similarly deprivation of God’s grace and succour wrecks one’s spiritual existence. A cursed person becomes so insensitive that he loses the ability to distinguish between truth and untruth. He fails to recognize and accept explicit signs and cannot differentiate between absurd argumentation and logical argument.

56.text:
Expanding the warning of the fifty-fifth verse that Hell is sufficient as a blaze, the fifty-sixth verse states the universal law of retribution awaiting everyone who rejects the signs and revelations of Allah. "Surely those who reject Our signs, We will cast them into the Fire" warns that those who deny the verses of the Qur'an and the clear proofs brought by Allah's Messengers will be brought into an encompassing Fire that surrounds every part of their bodies. "Whenever their skin is burnt completely, We will replace it so they will constantly taste the punishment. Indeed" reveals why the torment of the Hereafter never dulls or ends as worldly fire does when it destroys the nerves and consumes the body: in the Fire of Judgment, each time the skin is roasted through and consumed by the blaze, Allah restores it with a fresh new skin so that the sensation of punishment remains sharp and continuous without death or relief; and "Allah is Almighty, All-Wise" seals the verse by pairing the irresistible power of the Almighty, for whom recreating skins again and again is effortless and from whose grasp no wrongdoer can escape, with the perfect wisdom of the All-Wise who proportions every punishment justly to persistent denial, so that every soul who hears of the skins being renewed seventy thousand times a day understands that rejecting the signs of Allah out of pride and stubbornness leads to a torment that no human endurance can bear, before the fifty-seventh verse sets the eternal joy of the believers side by side with this warning.

**Casting those who reject Allah's revelations into the encompassing Fire.**

Surely those who disbelieve in Our signs — We shall expose them We shall admit them to a Fire wherein they shall burn; as often as their skins are consumed burnt We shall replace them with other skins restoring them to their initial unburnt state that they may taste the chastisement that they may suffer its severity. (Lo! Those who disbelieve Our revelations) Muhammad and the Qur'an, (We shall expose them to the Fire) in the Hereafter. Surely, those who disbelieved in Our Ayat, We shall burn them in Fire. Allah describes the torment in the Fire of Jahannam for those who disbelieve in His Ayat and hinder from the path of His Messengers. (Surely, those who disbelieved in Our Ayat ,) meaning, We will place them in the Fire which will encompass every part of their bodies. Stated now is the reward and punishment of a believer and a disbeliever as a universal rule. "Lightest in punishment among the people of fire will be the man in the sole of whose feet there will be two smoldering embers the heat from which will keep his brain boiling like a cauldron boiling to the brim. Surely those who disbelieve in Our signs-We shall expose them to a fire; as often as their skins are consumed We shall replace them with other skins that they may taste the chastisement. He causes them to remain in a state of insignificance yuqīmuhum bi-waṣfi al-ṣighār and leaves them to the estrangement of denial wa-yabqiyahum fī waḥshati al-inkār. Whenever something appears to their hearts from this story their rejection leads them to abandon faith in it and to dismiss its people with contempt so they are punished over and over again.

**Replacing burnt skins with fresh skins so they continually feel the torment.**

(As often as their skins are consumed) by the Fire (We shall exchange them for fresh skins that they may taste the torment) so that they feel the torment. Whenever their skins have been burned, they will be replaced with fresh skins, so that they continue to feel the punishment. As often as their skins are roasted through, We shall change them for other skins that they may taste the punishment. (We shall burn them in Fire. As often as their skins are roasted through, We shall change them for other skins that they may taste the punishment). Al-A'mash said that Ibn 'Umar said, "When their skin are burned, they will be given another skin in replacement, and this skin will be as white as paper. (As often as their skins are roasted through,) "Their skin will be roasted through, seventy thousand times every day. (As often as their skins are roasted through,) means, "Whenever the Fire has roasted them through and consumed their flesh, they will be told, 'Go back as you were before,' and they will." Explaining the highly apocalyptic statement in verse 56, Sayyidna Mu adh says that as soon as their skin is burnt out it will be replaced - and this will be with such speed that the skin will be replaced a hundred times in one moment. "The fire will eat them everyday seventy thousand times. When it would have eaten them up, they will be commanded: 'Return’.

**The might and wisdom of Allah in His judgment of those who reject truth.**

Surely God is ever Mighty nothing being beyond His power Wise in His creation. (Lo! Allah is ever Mighty) by taking vengeance on them, (Wise) He ruled that burnt skins be exchanged for fresh ones. Allah is Mighty, and nothing detracts from His might. And He is Wise in His administration and decree. Truly, Allah is Ever Most Powerful, All-Wise But those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, We shall admit them to Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise), abiding therein forever. (But those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, We shall admit them to Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise), abiding therein forever.) describing the destination of the happy ones in the gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow in all of its areas, spaces and corners, wherever they desire and wish.
