On the other hand, the existence of non-believers around them poses no such challenge and, therefore, their attitude towards them remains lax. But the preacher of truth cannot expect any leniency from them, for they become infuriated with jealousy over someone else having been granted religious representation, when they alone had formerly had a monopoly of religion. They quite forget that God chooses the representatives of His religion on the basis of purity of soul, inner piety and a sound heart, and not because of any outward show of piety. Just as starvation and thirst wreck one’s physical existence, similarly deprivation of God’s grace and succour wrecks one’s spiritual existence. A cursed person becomes so insensitive that he loses the ability to distinguish between truth and untruth. He fails to recognize and accept explicit signs and cannot differentiate between absurd argumentation and logical argument.

57.text:
Following the Qur'an's constant method of pairing warning with glad tidings, the fifty-seventh verse sets the everlasting home of the people of faith and righteous deeds directly opposite the burning Fire of the fifty-sixth verse. "As for those who believe and do good, We will admit them into Gardens under which rivers flow" promises everyone who joins true faith in Allah, His Messengers, and His Books to sincere righteous action that they will be welcomed into the gardens of Paradise beneath whose trees and lofty dwellings rivers of water, milk, honey, and pure drink flow wherever they wish. "to stay there for ever and ever" reinforces the permanence of their bliss with an emphatic double assurance of eternity: unlike the fleeting pleasures of this world, the life of Paradise knows neither death nor departure, nor any wish ever to leave. "There they will have pure spouses" crowns the garden's delights with companions purified of every physical impurity, illness, and bodily blemish as well as every flaw of character or temper. "and We will place them under a vast shade" closes the picture in direct contrast to the scorching heat of the fifty-sixth verse: an expansive, deep, never-receding shade beneath the trees of Paradise and the care of the Merciful where neither sun nor heat ever intrudes, where those who stood under the shade of obedience and faithfulness to Allah's commands in this brief life rest forever under the shade of His generosity, protection, and nearness in the world to come, before the fifty-eighth verse returns to the laws of public and private trust on earth.

**Admitting those who believe and do righteous deeds into eternal Gardens.**

And those that believe and perform righteous deeds We shall admit them to Gardens underneath which rivers flow wherein they abide they shall have therein spouses purified of menstruation and every impurity and We shall admit them to plenteous shade that is everlasting shade never replaced by any sun and this is the shade of Paradise. (And as for those who believe) in Muhammad, the Qur'an and in all Scriptures and messengers (and do good works) acts of obedience, i.e. they sincerely perform that which is between them and their Lord, (We shall make them enter) in the Hereafter (Gardens beneath which) beneath its trees and walls (rivers) rivers of wine, milk, honey and water (flow to dwell therein for ever) dwelling in Paradise, never to die or be removed; (there for them) in Paradise (are pure companions) they are pure from menstruation and filth (and We shall make them enter plenteous shade) a protected retreat; and it is also said that this means: an extended shade. Those who have faith in Allah and follow His messengers, doing good actions, will be entered on the Day of Judgement into gardens with rivers flowing beneath their palaces, where they will live eternally. Truly, Allah is Ever Most Powerful, All-Wise But those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, We shall admit them to Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise), abiding therein forever. (But those who believe and do deeds of righteousness, We shall admit them to Gardens under which rivers flow (Paradise), abiding therein forever.) describing the destination of the happy ones in the gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow in all of its areas, spaces and corners, wherever they desire and wish. They will reside in it for eternity, and they will not be transferred or removed from it, nor would they want to move from it. Stated now is the reward and punishment of a believer and a disbeliever as a universal rule. This is like saying: or which indicate that the blessings of Paradise will last forever.

**Spouses purified of every physical and moral blemish.**

In these gardens there will be mates for them, purified from any impurity, and they will be entered into expansive refreshing shade. Therein they shall have Azwajun Mutahharatun (purified mates), and We shall admit them to shades, wide and ever deepening. (Therein they shall have Azwajun Mutahharatun (purified mates),) free of menstruation, postnatal bleeding, filth, bad manners and shortcomings. Ibn 'Abbas said that the Ayah means, "They are purified of filth and foul things. The women of Jannah will be pure, that is, pure from menstruation, defecation, urination and nasal mucus. They shall also be 'pure and free from procreation and seminal impurity.' (Mazhari)

**Entering vast, everlasting shade and the shade of divine care.**

(And We shall admit them to shades, wide and ever deepening (Paradise).) means, wide, extensive, pure and elegant shade. (There is a tree in Paradise, that if a rider travels under its shade for a hundred years, he will not cross it. It is the Tree of Everlasting Life.) Here, by mentioning after it has been mentioned that the shade in Jannah will be dense and ever-present. If a rider were to ride under its shade for a hundred years, he will still not cross it. "That is the shade of the Throne (al-'arsh) which will never decline." And those that believe and perform righteous deeds We shall admit them to gardens underneath which rivers flow wherein they abide: they shall have therein spouses purified and We shall admit them to plenteous shade. Today they are in the shade of [God's] care riʿāya and tomorrow in the shade of [His] protection ḥimāya and sufficiency kifāya. Indeed they are in the shade of solicitude ʿināya in this world and the next. There are those who are in the shade of His mercy those who are in the shade of His care those who are in the shade of His special generosity those who are in the shade of His solicitude and those who are in the shade of His nearness. In real life, the hypocrites tread the path of selfish desires and give in to satanic inducements, but outwardly, bearing the label of religion, they think that their actions are truly guided by God’s religion. But the preacher of truth cannot expect any leniency from them, for they become infuriated with jealousy over someone else having been granted religious representation, when they alone had formerly had a monopoly of religion. They quite forget that God chooses the representatives of His religion on the basis of purity of soul, inner piety and a sound heart, and not because of any outward show of piety. Just as starvation and thirst wreck one’s physical existence, similarly deprivation of God’s grace and succour wrecks one’s spiritual existence.

58.text:
Moving from the eternal recompense of the Hereafter back to the moral foundations of community life, the fifty-eighth verse lays down the twin pillars of trustworthiness and just judgment for both rulers and ordinary citizens. "Indeed, Allah commands you to return trusts to their rightful owners" was revealed on the day of the Conquest of Makkah when the Prophet took the key of the Ka'bah from its hereditary custodian Uthman ibn Talhah, entered the House, and then came out reciting this verse to hand the key back to Uthman and his descendants forever rather than giving it to his own relatives who had requested it, while its general wording encompasses every trust: the rights of Allah in worship, the appointment of qualified and honest people to public office, and every deposit, property, or secret entrusted by one human being to another. "and when you judge between people, judge with fairness" commands everyone entrusted with leadership or called upon to arbitrate a dispute to decide with complete impartiality in line with Allah's law, whether between friend and foe or rich and poor. "What a noble commandment from Allah to you! Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing" praises the beauty of this divine instruction and reminds every trustee and judge that Allah hears every word spoken in court and sees every hidden act of fidelity or betrayal, showing that in Islam every public office, every judicial seat, every religious duty, and every private deposit or confidence is a sacred trust that will be answered for on the Day of Resurrection when even the hornless sheep takes its right from the horned sheep, and that a single day of just judgment in truth and fairness outweighs years of private devotion; whether the trust is the key of the Ka'bah returned to 'Uthman ibn Talhah at the conquest of Makkah in spite of past hostility, a public office bestowed on the most qualified and God-fearing person rather than on relatives or flatterers, or a daily financial transaction between two neighbors, fulfilling trusts and judging with justice form the twin pillars on which human society stands, prospers, and enjoys lasting security and peace under the watchful eye of its Creator, while the fifty-ninth verse sets out the duty of obedience and how disputes are resolved.

**The occasion of revelation concerning Uthman ibn Talhah and the key of the Ka'bah.**

Verily God commands you to restore trusts that is the rights entrusted to you by others back to their owners this was revealed when ‘Alī may God be pleased with him took the key of the Ka‘ba from its keeper ‘Uthmān b. Talha al-Hajabī by force upon the arrival of the Prophet s in Makkah in the year of the Conquest after he ‘Uthmān had tried to prevent him ‘Alī from taking it saying ‘If I had known that he was the Messenger of God I would not have prevented him’. The Messenger of God s then ordered him ‘Alī to give it back to him ‘Uthmān saying to him ‘Here you are it is yours now and always’. He ‘Uthmān was amazed by this whereupon ‘Alī recited to him this verse and he accepted Islam. Upon his death he ‘Uthmān gave it the key to his brother Shayba and thus it remained in the keep of his descendants. Although the verse was revealed regarding a specific occasion it holds true in general on account of the plural person to which it is addressed. Regarding the key that the Prophet ﷺ took from 'Uthman Ibn Talhah as a deposit, Allah commanded His Messenger to give back deposits to their owner, saying: (Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits) to give back the key (to their owners) to 'Uthman Ibn Talhah, (and, if ye judge between mankind) between 'Uthman Ibn Talhah and 'Abbas Ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, (that you judge justly) that you give back to 'Uthman and the providing of water (siqaya) to al-'Abbas. O Messenger of Allah! give me both the key and the providing of water, (Seer) of what 'Uthman Ibn Talhah did when he refused to give the key and said: Ibn Jarir recorded that Ibn Jurayj said about this Ayah, "It was revealed concerning 'Uthman bin Talhah from whom the Messenger of Allah took the key of the Ka'bah and entered it on the Day of the victory of Makkah. Ibn Jarir also narrated that 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said, "When the Messenger of Allah went out of the Ka'bah, he was reciting this Ayah,. But, the Holy Qur'an has, in this verse, taken into consideration the nature of trust involved therein, and directed the Holy Prophet to return the key to none else but Uthman, although, that was a time when Sayyidna Abbas and Sayyidna ALI had both requested that, since Baytullah's offices of water supply and custodial services (Siqaya and Sidana) were in their respective charge, this service of the Key-Bearer of the Ka'bah may be entrusted to them.

**Returning all trusts to their rightful owners and assigning public offices to the qualified.**

Allah instructs you, O believers, to return things in your care to the people who own them. Verily, Allah commands that you should render back the trusts to those, to whom they are due; and that when you judge between men, you judge with justice. This command refers to all things that one is expected to look after, such as Allah's rights on His servants: praying, Zakah, fasting, penalties for sins, vows and so forth. The command also includes the rights of the servants on each other, such as what they entrust each other with, including the cases that are not recorded or documented. (The rights will be rendered back to those to whom they are due, and even the sheep that does not have horns will take revenge from the horned sheep.) The Holy Qur'an says: ‌ It means: 'Surely, Allah commands you to fulfill trust obligations towards those entitled to them.' As to who is the addressee of this command, there are two probabilities: The functional outcome of the command in the verse is that everyone who holds anything in trust with him is duty-bound to see that trust obligations are faithfully fulfilled and that the rightful recipients have in their hands what is their due. According to narrations from Sayyidna Abu Hurairah and Sayyidna Ibn Umar appearing in al-Bukhari and Muslim, the Holy Prophet while describing the signs of hypocrisy on a certain day, pointed out to a particular sign which was: 'Give him an amanah and he will do khiyanah.' It means when an hypocrite is charged with a trust obligation, he will commit a breach of trust. Specially worth-remembering in this verse is that Allah Almighty has, by equating offices of the government with the trust obligations, made it clear at the very outset that amanah or whatever is held in trust should be handed over, properly and duly, to the person who is its rightful owner. But, they must be handed over to those who are its rightful, deserving recipients, those who have the ability to do what is required of them, have the qualification, the capability, and are clearly the best of those suitable and available for this office, and finally, are clearly superior to those in line in terms of their honesty and trustworthiness. In this verse the lovingly kind Lord, the generous and right-knowing, the care-taker of the servants, commands His servants to give back trusts. " In other words, do not intervene in them, and avoid betrayal, for after the faith and recognition of the servant, there is no attribute greater than holding in trust; and after unbelief, there is no attribute uglier than betrayal. Holding in trust is the pillar of the religion, the per fection of tawḤīd, and the attribute of the prophets and the angels. In the firm text of the revealed book, the Lord of the Worlds describes Gabriel by saying, "brought down by the trustworthy spirit" [26:193]. And in describing Joseph the sincerely truthful He says, quoting the king of Egypt, "Surely today with us thou art emplaced, trustworthy" [12:54]. MuṣṬafā said, "You have taken them as a trust from God, and you have made their private parts lawful to you by God's word. " Third is the property you leave with someone, or the secret you tell to him, for that is a trust.

**Judging between people with fairness under the gaze of the All-Hearing, All-Seeing.**

Excellent is ni‘immā the mīm of ni‘ima has been assimilated with the indefinite particle mā which is the object described in other words na‘ima shay’an ‘an excellent thing is’ the admonition God gives you to restore a trust and to judge with justice. God is ever Hearer of what is said Seer of what is done. (Lo! comely is this which Allah admonisheth you) comely is this which Allah commands you, of giving back deposits to their owners and judging justly. He instructs you, if you judge between people in any matter, to judge between them with justice according to His sacred laws. Allah’s laws in every situation for you are, of course, excellent. Allah hears all that you say and sees all that you do. Muhammad bin Ka'b, Zayd bin Aslam and Shahr bin Hawshab said; "This Ayah was revealed about those in authority", meaning those who judge between people. (Allah is with the judge as long as he does not commit injustice, for when he does, Allah will make him reliant on himself.) A statement goes, "One day of justice equals forty years of worship. (Verily, how excellent is the teaching which He (Allah) gives you!) meaning, His commands to return the trusts to their owners, to judge between people with justice, and all of His complete, perfect and great commandments and laws. (Truly, Allah is Ever All-Hearer, All-Seer.) means, He hears your statements and knows your actions. This does not take into consideration the leeway that exists here too, very much like it is in the first sentence, that is, the probability exists that both office-holders and masses are included in this address for the simple reason that among the common people at large the usual practice is to appoint a neutral arbitrator to judge and decide between disputing parties. According to another hadith, the Holy Prophet said to his noble Companions: 'Do you know who will be the first to go under the shade of Allah?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know this best.' Then, he said: 'These will be people who, when truth appears, hasten to accept it; and when asked, they spend their wealth; and when they judge (between people), they do it as fairly as they would have done for themselves.'. Every responsibility is a trust which must be properly discharged. Our dealings with everyone should be just and fair, no matter whether they be friend or foe. Even if the way of trustworthiness and justice appears to run counter to one’s interests and worldly considerations, one has to adhere to the path of justice and truth. If there are opportunities of forming the government, the Muslims must establish a proper Islamic government, but if such opportunities do not exist, they should concentrate on leading a religious life under the guidance of reliable persons selected from among themselves.

59.text:
Having commanded rulers and trustees in the fifty-eighth verse to fulfil trusts and judge with justice, the fifty-ninth verse addresses the whole believing community to establish the constitutional order of Islam. "O believers! Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you" sets out the hierarchy of obedience: absolute obedience to Allah in His Book and to His Messenger in his Sunnah, and obedience to the legitimate leaders, commanders, and scholars of the Muslims in all that is right, while repeating the verb obey for Allah and for the Messenger but not for those in authority to show that no human leader may ever be obeyed in disobedience to Allah, as demonstrated when a commander in anger ordered his troop to step into a fire and the Prophet praised them for refusing a sinful command. "Should you disagree on anything, then refer it to Allah and His Messenger, if you truly believe in Allah and the Last Day" provides the supreme rule whenever believers or their leaders differ over any matter of religion or law: returning the dispute to the Book of Allah and the living Sunnah of His Messenger as the test of genuine faith in Allah and the Last Day. "This is the best and fairest resolution" seals the verse by affirming that abiding by revelation brings the purest harmony in this world and the best outcome in the Hereafter, so that neither rulers become tyrants above the law nor citizens fall into lawless division, because both the leader and the led stand together under the supreme sovereignty of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, where every disagreement finds a clean, authoritative, and blessed settlement that unites hearts in this world and earns the richest reward when everyone returns to stand before Allah in the Hereafter, whereas obeying any creature in disobedience to the Creator or refusing the judgment of the Book and the Prophet tears the community apart, destroys social trust, and forfeits the blessing of faith in both worlds, before the sixtieth verse exposes the hypocrites who sought judgment from false judges instead.

**Obeying Allah, the Messenger, and those in authority within obedience to Allah.**

(Obey Allah) in that which He has commanded you, (and obey the messenger) in that which he commands you (and those of you who are in authority) the leaders of military expeditions; it also said that this means: the men of sacred knowledge; (and if ye have a dispute concerning any matter, refer it to Allah) to the Book of Allah (and the messenger) and to the practice of the Messenger (if you are (in truth) believers in Allah and the Last Day) resurrection after death. O you who have faith, follow Allah and His Messenger: doing what they instruct and staying away from what they prohibit, and follow those in authority, as long as they do not instruct you to do wrong. (Obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and those of you who are in authority.) "Was revealed about 'Abdullah bin Hudhafah bin Qays bin 'Adi, who the Messenger of Allah sent on a military expedition. When they left, he became angry with them for some reason and said to them, 'Has not the Messenger of Allah commanded you to obey me?' They said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Collect some wood,' and then he started a fire with the wood, saying, 'I command you to enter the fire.' The people almost entered the fire, but a young man among them said, 'You only ran away from the Fire to Allah's Messenger. Therefore, do not rush until you go back to Allah's Messenger, and if he commands you to enter it, then enter it.' When they went back to Allah's Messenger , they told him what had happened, and the Messenger said,. (The Muslim is required to hear and obey in that which he likes and dislikes, unless he was commanded to sin. When he is commanded with sin, then there is no hearing or obeying.) This Hadith is recorded in the Two Sahihs. 'Ubadah bin As-Samit said, "We gave our pledge to Allah's Messenger to hear and obey (our leaders), while active and otherwise, in times of ease and times of difficulty, even if we were deprived of our due shares, and to not dispute this matter (leadership) with its rightful people. (Even if a slave was appointed over you, and he rules you with Allah's Book, then listen to him and obey him.) Muslim recorded this Hadith. (Whoever obeys me, obeys Allah, and whoever disobeys me, disobeys Allah. Whoever obeys my commander, obeys me, and whoever disobeys my commander, disobeys me.) This is why Allah said,. (And those of you who are in authority) in the obedience to Allah which they command you, not what constitutes disobedience of Allah, for there is no obedience to anyone in disobedience to Allah, as we mentioned in the authentic Hadith,. It was revealed about Hudhafah ibn Qays ibn Adiyy who was sent by the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, in a military expedition . The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace, sent Khalid ibn al-Walid in a military expedition to one of the Arab clans. When he drew closer to them at night, he stopped to camp in order to try to conquer them the following morning. Meanwhile this clan was warned about the approaching military expedition which made them flee the area, except for one man who was a Muslim. This man asked his family to get ready to move and then he went to the camp of Khalid and entered in on Ammar. The following morning, Khalid invaded the clan but found no one except this man, and so he imprisoned him and seized his property. Let the man go, for he is a Muslim and I have already given him amnesty and told him to stay .

**Referring every dispute back to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.**

If you should quarrel disagree about anything refer it to God that is to His Book and the Messenger while he lives and thereafter refer to his Sunna in other words examine these disputes with reference to these two sources if you believe in God and the Last Day; that reference to the two sources is better for you than quarrelling or adhering to personal opinions and more excellent in interpretation in the end. (That) referring the matter to the Book of Allah and the practice of His Messenger (is better and more seemly in the end). If you disagree about something, then refer it to Allah’s revelation and the traditions of His Prophet ﷺ, if you have faith in Allah and the Last Day. Mujahid and several others among the Salaf said that the Ayah means, "(Refer) to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger." This is a command from Allah that whatever areas the people dispute about, whether major or minor areas of the religion, they are required to refer to the Qur'an and Sunnah for judgment concerning these disputes. (And in whatsoever you differ, the decision thereof is with Allah). [42:10] Therefore, whatever the Book and Sunnah decide and testify to the truth of, then it, is the plain truth. (if you believe in Allah and in the Last Day.) meaning, refer the disputes and conflicts that arise between you to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger for judgment. (if you believe in Allah and in the Last Day.) indicates that those who do not refer to the Book and Sunnah for judgment in their disputes, are not believers in Allah or the Last Day. Finally, let us now refer to the statement: ‌ ‌ in verse 59 (Then, if you quarrel about something, revert it back to Allah and the Messenger.) Revert to ahkam, the code of commands as mandated in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah. If the textually-mandated ahkam do not exist, the act of reverting back will be accomplished by analogical deduction (Qiyas) as based on their precedents.

**Why returning to revelation is better and produces the fairest outcome.**

Referring to the revelation and the traditions is better than continuing in your disagreements and in giving mere opinions, and will bring about the best result for you. Our dealings with everyone should be just and fair, no matter whether they be friend or foe. Even if the way of trustworthiness and justice appears to run counter to one’s interests and worldly considerations, one has to adhere to the path of justice and truth. Our gain lies in following not the dictates of the self, but the directives of God. If there are opportunities of forming the government, the Muslims must establish a proper Islamic government, but if such opportunities do not exist, they should concentrate on leading a religious life under the guidance of reliable persons selected from among themselves. Any differences between them should be resolved in the light of instructions given by God and the Prophet. Everyone does have the right to differ, but no one is permitted to defy a collective decision. If you should quarrel about anything refer it to God and the Messenger if you believe in God and the Last Day; that is better and more excellent in interpretation. He compares obedience to Him with obedience to the Messenger hon oring his affair and elevating his status. According to the explanation of deeper knowl edge maʿrifa the one who has deeper knowledge ʿārif has authority dhū l-amr over the one who is just starting out. It is said that the friend and guardian walī of the aspirant is better awlā for the aspirant than the aspirant [himself]. In scholarly lan guage this means the Book and the sunna. [But] according to the explana tion of God's unity bayān al-tawḥīd it is to commit and entrust knowledge of [the matter] to God . When two conflicting inclinations arise in the heart of a believer and [the believer] has [access to] the reasoning provided by religious scholars he can contemplate what he understands from their understanding. A master of the heart [on the other hand] entrusts [the matter] to the Real and pays heed to what is said to him in his inner most self and what has been cast into his heart without any intermediary.

60.text:
Immediately after the fifty-ninth verse made referring disputes to Allah and His Messenger the condition of true faith, the sixtieth verse unmasks the hypocrisy of those who professed Islam with their tongues while running to corrupt worldly arbiters whenever they knew the law of Allah would rule against them. "Have you O Prophet not seen those who claim they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you?" calls attention to the men who claimed to believe in the Qur'an and in the earlier Scriptures, yet exposed the emptiness of their claim as soon as a real dispute arose over property or rights. "They seek the judgment of false judges, which they were commanded to reject" recounts how, in a dispute between a Jewish man and a hypocrite named Bishr, the Jewish man asked to go before the Prophet because he knew the Messenger would never take a bribe or judge unjustly, whereas the hypocrite demanded they go to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf or a pre-Islamic soothsayer because he knew his case was false, turning for judgment to taghut, every false authority and un-Islamic tribunal that Allah had commanded them to renounce. "And Satan only desires to lead them farther away" closes the verse by naming the true author of that flight from divine justice: Satan lures people away from the court of revelation so as to cast them so far from the straight path that they never find their way back, proving that true faith is tested not by empty words in times of ease, but by whether a person willingly submits to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger even when that judgment goes against his own desires and financial interest; for anyone who claims to believe in revealed scripture yet runs to corrupt tribunals, pre-Islamic customs, or partial arbiters whenever the truth does not favor his greed is in reality answering the call of Satan, who lures people step by step away from the straight path until they cannot find their way back; whether the false judge is a pre-Islamic soothsayer, a corrupt tribal chief, or any man-made system preferred out of greed over the clear ruling of Allah, turning to it exposes the emptiness of a purely verbal claim to faith and shows that the heart has not yet surrendered to its Lord, a refusal that the sixty-first verse follows as they turn away in open aversion.

**Claiming faith in revelation while taking disputes to Taghut.**

Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you desiring to take their disputes to a false deity tāghūt one excessive in tempting others to falsehood tughyān namely Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf when they have been commanded to renounce him? and not to associate with him. (Hast thou not seen) have you not been informed, O Muhammad, about (those who pretend that they believe in that which is revealed unto thee) i.e. the Qur'an (and that which was revealed before thee) i.e. the Torah, (how they would go for judgement (in their disputes) to false deities) Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf (when they have been ordered) in the Qur'an (to abjure them?) to disavow them. Have you not seen, O Messenger, the contradiction of the hypocrites among the Jews, who claim falsely that they have faith in what was revealed to you and in what was revealed to the messengers before you, but in resolving their disagreements want to refer back to what Allah has not legislated, and what people have invented, when they were instructed to reject such things. Have you not seen those (hyprocrites) who claim that they believe in that which has been sent down to you, and that which was sent down before you, and they wish to go for judgment (in their disputes) to the Taghut while they have been ordered to reject them. Allah chastises those who claim to believe in what Allah has sent down to His Messenger and to the earlier Prophets, yet they refer to other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger for judgment in various disputes. " It was also reported that the Ayah was revealed about some hypocrites who pretended to be Muslims, yet they sought to refer to the judgment of Jahiliyyah. However, the Ayah has a general meaning, as it chastises all those who refrain from referring to the Qur'an and Sunnah for judgment and prefer the judgment of whatever they chose of falsehood, which befits the description of Taghut here. The first verse exposes the claim of those who say that they have believed in earlier scriptures, the Torah and the Evangel, and now believe in the Book (the Qur'an) revealed to the Holy Prophet Muhammad . That is, earlier in time, they were a part of the community of the people of the Book, then they entered the fold of Islam and became a part of the Muslim community. Lexically, “ Taghut” primarily means one who exceeds the limits.' In usage, the Satan is referred to as Taghut. In this verse, carrying the dispute to Ka'b ibn Ashraf has been equated with carrying it to the Satan. The reason could be that Ka'b ibn Ashraf was himself a satan personified, or it could be that bypassing a decision under the God-given law and preferring a decision contrary to it can only come from the teaching of the Satan.

**The dispute between the hypocrite and the Jew and the occasions of revelation.**

The following verse was revealed when a Jew and a hypocrite fell into a dispute. The hypocrite called on Ka‘b b. al-Ashraf to arbitrate between them while the Jew called on the Prophet s. When they came to him the Prophet ruled in favour of the Jew. But the hypocrite was not satisfied and so they went before ‘Umar. The Jew told him what had happened whereupon he ‘Umar turned to the hypocrite and asked him ‘Is this true?’ and when he replied ‘Yes’ he ‘Umar killed him. This verse was revealed about a hypocrite by the name of Bishr whom 'Umar Ibn al-Khattab had killed. It was a strange coincidence that a Jew would leave his chief aside and elect to go by the judgment of the Holy Prophet while Bishr, who called himself a Muslim, would bypass him and elect to go by the judgment of the Jewish chief. Both of them were certain that the Holy Prophet will give a judgment which is bound to be true and just. Bishr, the hypocrite was in the wrong, therefore, he knew that the Prophet's judgment will be against him - even though he claimed to be a Muslim while his adversary was a Jew. However, after some mutual cross talk between them, both of them agreed upon the option of going to the Holy Prophet and requesting him to give a decision in their dispute. He was not pleased with this judgment, so he hit upon a new plan to persuade the Jew to somehow agree to go to Sayyidna Umar ibn al-Khattab and have him give a decision in their case. The Jew told him everything about the incident and also narrated to him how the Holy Prophet had already given his decision in this case and that this man was not satisfied with it and had, therefore, brought his case before you.' Sayyidna Umar asked Bishr, "Is this what really happened? Abu Burdah al-Aslami was a soothsayer who used to settle the disputes that the Jews had amongst themselves. When a group of people from Aslam took their dispute to him, Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Hast thou not seen those who pretend) up to his saying ( were seeking naught but harmony and kindness) [4:62] . We were told that this verse was revealed about a dispute regarding a certain property in which were involved a man from the Helpers called Qays and a Jewish man. They took their dispute to a soothsayer in Medina to judge between them while leaving the Prophet of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace. In fact the Jew was urging the Muslim to take their dispute to the Prophet of Allah, because he knew he will not wrong him. But the Helper refused to, even though he was a Muslim, and insisted to go to the soothsayer. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse censoring the person who was pretending to be Muslim as well as the Jew who belonged to the people of the Book, saying (Hast thou not seen those who pretend that they believe in that which is revealed unto thee) up to His words ( thou seest the hypocrites turn from thee with aversion) [4:61] . The Jew invited the hypocrite to take their dispute to the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, because he knew that he did not accept bribery. The hypocrite, on the other hand, called the Jewish man to take their dispute to their own arbiters because he knew that they took bribery for the judgments they issued.

**How Satan desires to lead those who abandon divine judgment far astray.**

But Satan desires to mislead them far astray from the truth. (Satan would mislead them far astray) from the Truth and guidance. Satan wants to lead them far away from the truth, and they will not be guided through this. But Shaytan wishes to lead them far astray And when it is said to them: "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion How then, when a catastrophe befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, they come to you swearing by Allah, "We meant no more than goodwill and conciliation! They (hypocrites) are those of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts; so turn aside from them (do not punish them) but admonish them, and speak to them an effective word to reach their inner selves. (How then, when a catastrophe befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth,) meaning, how about it if they feel compelled to join you because of disasters that they suffer due to their sins, then they will be in need of you. (They come to you swearing by Allah, "We meant no more than goodwill and conciliation!") apologizing and swearing that they only sought goodwill and reconciliation when they referred to other than the Prophet for judgment, not that they believe in such alternative judgment, as they claim. These people are hypocrites, and Allah knows what is in their hearts and will punish them accordingly, for nothing escapes Allah's watch. Our dealings with everyone should be just and fair, no matter whether they be friend or foe. Even if the way of trustworthiness and justice appears to run counter to one’s interests and worldly considerations, one has to adhere to the path of justice and truth. Our gain lies in following not the dictates of the self, but the directives of God. If there are opportunities of forming the government, the Muslims must establish a proper Islamic government, but if such opportunities do not exist, they should concentrate on leading a religious life under the guidance of reliable persons selected from among themselves. Any differences between them should be resolved in the light of instructions given by God and the Prophet. Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you desiring to take their disputes to a false deity when they have been commanded to renounce himḍ But Satan desires to mislead them far astray. Outwardly they proclaimed sincerity while acting hypocritically in secret. He exposed them through the tongue of Gabriel saying desir ing to take their disputes to a false deity when they have been commanded to renounce him yakfurū bihi that is reject him. Whoever abandons his path and returns to anyone other than his master ustādh becomes deserving of exclusion and condemnation.

61.text:
Continuing the sixtieth verse's exposure of those who claimed faith while seeking judgment from false arbiters, the sixty-first verse shows how they behave the moment they are invited back to the word of God and the court of His Prophet. "When it is said to them" captures the sincere call addressed to a disputant in Medina—even, in one famous case, by his Jewish opponent who knew that the Prophet never took bribes or wronged anyone—inviting him to settle their quarrel by divine law. "Come to Allah’s revelations and to the Messenger" summons them to the clear rulings sent down in the Qur'an and to the living judgment of the Messenger whom Allah appointed to decide between people in truth. Instead of welcoming that impartial standard, "you see the hypocrites turn away from you stubbornly" exposes their true inward state: because their claim is flimsy and they want a decision that serves their greed rather than justice, they turn their backs in arrogance and aversion, proving that anyone who refuses the judgment of Allah and His Messenger when it goes against his personal interest is empty of real faith, whatever fine words he uses to justify himself, since everything other than the word of truth is easy for hypocrites to hear while their hearts flee from the light of the Prophet's court just as the eye of the bat flees the light of the sun, before the sixty-second verse asks what they will do when disaster strikes them for their deeds.

**Turning away in aversion when called to the revelation and the Messenger.**

And when it is said to them ‘Come to what God has revealed as regards rulings in the Qur’ān and the Messenger’ that he may judge between you you see the hypocrites turn away from you vehemently to others. If these hypocrites are told to come to the law that Allah has revealed in His Scripture, and to the Messenger to judge between them in their disagreements, you will see them, O Messenger, turning away from you completely to others. (And then it is said unto them) to Hatib Ibn Abi Balta'ah, the hypocrite, who had a dispute with al-Zubayr Ibn al-'Awwam, the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ: (Come unto that which Allah hath revealed) come to the ruling which Allah has revealed in the Qur'an (and unto the messenger) and to the judgement of the messenger, (thou seest the hypocrites) Hatib Ibn Abi Balta'ah (turn from you with aversion) turn away from your judgement in complete rejection. (turn away from you with aversion) means, they turn away from you in arrogance, just as Allah described the polytheists,. These people are hypocrites, and Allah knows what is in their hearts and will punish them accordingly, for nothing escapes Allah's watch.

**Why refusing the judgment of the Prophet exposes hypocrisy in disputes.**

The second verse tells us that turning away from the decision of the Holy Prophet given under the dictates of the Shari’ ah in matters relating to mutual quarrels and disputes, can never be the response of a Muslim. One who does it has to be a munafiq (hypocrite). Thus, when the disbelief of this hypocrite was practically exposed through his dissatisfaction with the decision of the Holy Prophet his being killed by Sayyidna Umar became all the more justified, because he no more remained a munafiq (hypocrite) and, in fact, became an open Kafir (or apostate). During the early period of Madīnah there used to be two courts where judgement on controversial issues might be sought: one pre-dating Islam and controlled by the leaders of the Jews, and the other set up by the Prophet, established after the Migration. Those Muslims who were not ready to sacrifice their interests for the sake of religion and were aware that their cases were too flimsy to be awarded favourable decisions by the court of the Prophet, used to approach the court of Ka‘b ibn Ashraf, a leader of the Jews. Such an attitude is totally against the spirit of the faith. If an individual is unwilling to accept God’s judgement, and aspires to be favoured with a decision to his own liking, his claim to faith is false, whatever repertoire of beautiful words he may draw on to justify his stand. However, while avoiding confrontation with such people, efforts to reform them must be effectively continued.

**The dispute in Madinah and the blindness of hearts that follow whim.**

When a group of people from Aslam took their dispute to him, Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Hast thou not seen those who pretend) up to his saying ( were seeking naught but harmony and kindness) [4:62] . We were told that this verse was revealed about a dispute regarding a certain property in which were involved a man from the Helpers called Qays and a Jewish man. They took their dispute to a soothsayer in Medina to judge between them while leaving the Prophet of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace. Allah, exalted is He, rebuked them for doing so. In fact the Jew was urging the Muslim to take their dispute to the Prophet of Allah, because he knew he will not wrong him. But the Helper refused to, even though he was a Muslim, and insisted to go to the soothsayer. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse censoring the person who was pretending to be Muslim as well as the Jew who belonged to the people of the Book, saying (Hast thou not seen those who pretend that they believe in that which is revealed unto thee) up to His words ( thou seest the hypocrites turn from thee with aversion) [4:61] . It was reported that the reason behind revealing this Ayah was that a man from the Ansar and a Jew had a dispute, and the Jew said, "Let us refer to Muhammad to judge between us. Everything other than the word of the Real is easy for hypocrites [to hear]. [On the other hand] the declaration of God's unity is heard only by those who are sincere. Those who are listless and those who are hostile do not hear that which is true since it is difficult for those who are not sincere to oppose personal whims. Just as the eye of the bat is incapable of facing the sun the hypocrites were unable to stand firm before [the Prophet] and that was the cause of their vehemently turning away.

62.text:
Following the sixty-first verse's portrait of the hypocrites stubbornly turning away from the Prophet's court, the sixty-second verse exposes how quickly their arrogance collapses into false oaths once their scheming brings ruin upon their own heads. "How ˹horrible˺ will it be if a disaster strikes them because of what their hands have done" asks what state they will be in when disgrace, exposure, or punishment overtakes them as the direct fruit of their own sins, breach of trust, and refusal of divine judgment—whether through their secret plot coming out in the open, the punishment of their accomplice, or the misfortune that follows rebellion against Allah. Only when they are cornered by the consequences of their own actions, "then they come to you swearing by Allah" describes them hurrying back to the Messenger with solemn oaths in Allah's name to cover up their betrayal. Their excuse, "We intended nothing but goodwill and reconciliation," claims that in taking their dispute to other arbiters they never doubted the Prophet's station, but only wanted an easy compromise, mutual harmony, and a gentle patch-up rather than the strict, uncompromising truth of the law—a hollow plea that vanishes the moment the crisis passes, because the supplication and excuses of the insincere during moments of trouble have no root in the heart and last only until the storm blows over, whereas true goodness and lasting reconciliation between disputing parties can never be found by bypassing the sacred law of Allah and the impartial court of His Messenger for the crooked verdicts of those who take bribes, flatter the powerful, and twist justice to suit personal greed, tribal pride, and partisan advantage in this fleeting world, an excuse that the sixty-third verse answers by revealing that Allah knows everything hidden in their hearts.

**When disaster and affliction strike them for what their hands have done.**

How would it be what would they do when an affliction a punishment befalls them for what their own hands have sent before them of unbelief and acts of disobedience that is to say would they then be able to turn away and escape it? They then come to you thumma jā’ūka a supplement to yasuddūn ‘they turn away’ of the previous verse swearing by God that in turning to other than you for arbitration ‘We sought only virtue settlement and harmony’ reconciliation between the disputing parties by any approximate judgement without regard for the painful truth. (How would it be) what shall they do (if a misfortune) a punishment (smote them because of that which their own hands have sent before (them) because of turning away (they come unto you) after that, (swearing by Allah) i.e. Hatib swearing by Allah (that they were seeking naught) when they turned away (but harmony) in speech (and kindness) correctness. How would it be when an affliction befalls them for what their own hands have sent before them! They then come to you swearing by God that We sought only virtue and harmony. The beseeching of the insincere at the attacks of misfortune is without foundation. It deserves no consideration because it only lasts until the tribulation has passed. The greater affliction is being indifferent to the affliction [brought on by what their own hands have sent before them]. It is said that part of the affliction is being deprived [of the blessing] in the present moment by that which is of no use to you.

**Swearing by Allah that they sought only goodwill and harmony.**

Their plea, in gist, was that they did not bypass the Messenger of Allah for any reason of lack of belief in the truth of his station and mission and that they did not prefer the decision of others over his decisions as if it was the ultimate Truth. For instance, one such expedient consideration was that, a case going to the Messenger of Allah would have meant that the decision would have been strictly legal, true and just - devoid of any options of mutual patch-up and tolerance (of 'other' factors not necessarily just): As evident, they came up with all these interpretations only when their secret was revealed and their wickedness and hypocrisy came out in the open and their man was killed at the hands of Sayyidna Umar . In short, it was a consequence of their evil deed which brought upon them the disgrace or disaster of an accomplice killed, following which they started making statements on oath with all sorts of excuses and interpretations. Allah Almighty, in this verse, makes it very clear that these people are liars in their oaths and interpretations and that everything they have done, they have done because of their disbelief and hypocrisy. But they, as the verse says, would become all alert once they get into trouble as a result of their own evil deeds - like when the exposure of their breach of trust or hypocrisy brings shame on them, or when it leads to the killing of their man - then, they come to the Messenger swearing by Allah that they meant nothing but good. That they took their case to somebody else was not because they did not believe in the Prophet, or that they doubted the veracity of his judgment, but that their aim was to promote good and. bring about harmony between the disputing parties. How will their situation be when misfortunes come upon them because of the sins they have committed, and then they come to you, O Messenger, apologising and swearing by Allah that when they turned to other things to try and settle their disagreements they were only trying to do good and bring about reconciliation between the people who were disagreeing. What they say is false, and doing good involves following the rulings of Allah’s sacred law.

**False excuses after bypassing the Messenger for corrupt arbiters.**

When a group of people from Aslam took their dispute to him, Allah, exalted is He, revealed (Hast thou not seen those who pretend) up to his saying ( were seeking naught but harmony and kindness) [4:62] . We were told that this verse was revealed about a dispute regarding a certain property in which were involved a man from the Helpers called Qays and a Jewish man. They took their dispute to a soothsayer in Medina to judge between them while leaving the Prophet of Allah, Allah bless him and give him peace. In fact the Jew was urging the Muslim to take their dispute to the Prophet of Allah, because he knew he will not wrong him. And so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse censoring the person who was pretending to be Muslim as well as the Jew who belonged to the people of the Book, saying (Hast thou not seen those who pretend that they believe in that which is revealed unto thee) up to His words ( thou seest the hypocrites turn from thee with aversion) [4:61] . The Jew invited the hypocrite to take their dispute to the Prophet, Allah bless him and give him peace, because he knew that he did not accept bribery. The hypocrite, on the other hand, called the Jewish man to take their dispute to their own arbiters because he knew that they took bribery for the judgments they issued. Have you not seen those (hyprocrites) who claim that they believe in that which has been sent down to you, and that which was sent down before you, and they wish to go for judgment (in their disputes) to the Taghut while they have been ordered to reject them. They (hypocrites) are those of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts; so turn aside from them (do not punish them) but admonish them, and speak to them an effective word to reach their inner selves. These people are hypocrites, and Allah knows what is in their hearts and will punish them accordingly, for nothing escapes Allah's watch. During the early period of Madīnah there used to be two courts where judgement on controversial issues might be sought: one pre-dating Islam and controlled by the leaders of the Jews, and the other set up by the Prophet, established after the Migration. Those Muslims who were not ready to sacrifice their interests for the sake of religion and were aware that their cases were too flimsy to be awarded favourable decisions by the court of the Prophet, used to approach the court of Ka‘b ibn Ashraf, a leader of the Jews. If an individual is unwilling to accept God’s judgement, and aspires to be favoured with a decision to his own liking, his claim to faith is false, whatever repertoire of beautiful words he may draw on to justify his stand.

63.text:
Answering the false oaths and excuses of the sixty-second verse, the sixty-third verse strips away the hypocrites' cover and teaches the Prophet how to deal with them through a combination of forbearance and soul-piercing counsel. "˹Only˺ Allah knows what is in their hearts" sweeps aside their sworn claims of seeking harmony, because nothing escapes Allah's watch and He knows the hypocrisy, malice, and ulterior motives concealed inside their breasts, whether in bypassing the Prophet's court or in building a rival mosque under the pretense of kindness. Because their inward disease is fully known to God and their worldly schemes cannot harm His cause, "So turn away from them, caution them" instructs the Messenger to pass over their excuses without exacting immediate worldly punishment, while warning them squarely of the danger of their hypocrisy and of what lies beyond this present life. Finally, "and give them advice that will shake their very souls" commands him to speak to them in plain, penetrating, and moving words that reach their inner selves, reprimanding them and calling them to sincere repentance before their secret is exposed and punishment overtakes them, while the sixty-fourth verse reminds them that messengers are sent only to be obeyed and keeps open the door of forgiveness; for even when the hypocrites lie under oath and deserve exposure, the Prophet is taught to combine outward clemency with words of admonition that awaken fear of the Hereafter, warn them that Allah's knowledge encompasses every secret plot, and invite them to sincere faith before the day comes when no excuse is accepted.

**Allah knows the hypocrisy and ulterior motives hidden in their hearts.**

Those — God knows what is in their hearts in the way of hypocrisy and the mendacity of their excuses; so turn away from them with forgiveness and admonish them make them fear God and say to them regarding the issue of their souls penetrating words affecting them in other words reprimand them so that they repent of their unbelief. Allah knows what hypocrisy and ulterior motives these people hide in their hearts, so turn away from them, O Messenger, and make clear to them the laws of Allah: encouraging them to be loyal to Allah, making clear to them how wrong it is to turn away from Him, and advise them in a way that will move them. (Those are they) i.e. him who did turn away from the Prophet ﷺ (the secrets of whose hearts Allah knoweth) He knows the hypocrisy in the heart of Hatib Ibn Abi Balta'ah. How shall they do-those who established a counter mosque-when a punishment strikes them, because of the counter mosque they built, and then afterward came to you-Tha'labah and Hatib-swearing by Allah that they did not intend by the building of the mosque except kindness to the believers and religious harmony, so that you send us a man of knowledge to teach us? (So oppose them) leave them and do not punish them this time (and admonish them) with your words so that they do not do it again, (and address them in plain terms about their souls) threaten them in an unequivocal way that you will punish them if they do it again. They (hypocrites) are those of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts; so turn aside from them (do not punish them) but admonish them, and speak to them an effective word to reach their inner selves. These people are hypocrites, and Allah knows what is in their hearts and will punish them accordingly, for nothing escapes Allah's watch.

**Turning away from punishment while cautioning them with penetrating words.**

The fourth verse comes up with the answer. It says that Allah is all-aware of the disbelief and hypocrisy rooted in their hearts. All their interpretations are false, and their oaths, an exercise in lying. (but admonish them) means, advise them against the hypocrisy and evil that reside in their hearts,. **Reforming those whose claims to faith fail at the test of self-interest.**

During the early period of Madīnah there used to be two courts where judgement on controversial issues might be sought: one pre-dating Islam and controlled by the leaders of the Jews, and the other set up by the Prophet, established after the Migration. Those Muslims who were not ready to sacrifice their interests for the sake of religion and were aware that their cases were too flimsy to be awarded favourable decisions by the court of the Prophet, used to approach the court of Ka‘b ibn Ashraf, a leader of the Jews. Such an attitude is totally against the spirit of the faith. If an individual is unwilling to accept God’s judgement, and aspires to be favoured with a decision to his own liking, his claim to faith is false, whatever repertoire of beautiful words he may draw on to justify his stand. However, while avoiding confrontation with such people, efforts to reform them must be effectively continued. Moving from the conditional promise of the sixty-sixth through sixty-eighth verses to a universal glad tiding for every believer, the sixty-ninth verse answers the loving anxiety of Companions like Thawban who feared that in the Hereafter the Prophet would be raised so high above them that they would no longer be able to see him. "And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger will be in the company of those blessed by Allah: the prophets" promises that everyone who carries out the obligations of Allah and follows the practice of His Messenger will not be separated from those he loves, but will be gathered in the company of the highest recipients of divine grace, beginning with Muhammad and all the prophets. Alongside them stand "the people of truth, the martyrs," namely the truthful ones—headed by the foremost Companions whose inward and outward affirmation of the truth was complete without a shadow of doubt—and those who gave their lives as witnesses in the path of Allah. With them too are "and the righteous—what honourable company" embracing all who keep their inward and outward states upright and acclaiming the joy of visiting, seeing, and sitting with those four blessed ranks in Paradise, for as the Prophet assured his Companions when they wept at the thought of being parted from him in the world to come, a person will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with those whom he loves, and those in the higher chambers of Paradise will come down to visit and sit with those below them while those below will be granted leave to ascend and enjoy the warmth and honor of their blessed company forever in the Gardens of delight, before the seventieth verse reminds us that such companionship is pure grace from Allah.

**Obeying Allah and the Messenger brings companionship with the four blessed ranks.**

Whoever obeys God and the Messenger in what he commands they are with those whom God has blessed of the prophets and the truthful that is the most excellent of the Prophet’s Companions because of the fullness of their truthfulness and their affirmation of the truth; and the martyrs those slain in the path of God; and the righteous all those other than the ones mentioned. What fine companions they are! in Paradise since in it one will enjoy seeing them visiting them and being in their presence even though they will be in the highest stations in relation to others. Those who follow Allah and the Messenger will be with those whom Allah has blessed with entry into Paradise from amongst the prophets, the truthful ones whose acceptance of what the prophets brought was complete and who practised it, the martyrs who were killed in Allah’s path, and the righteous whose outward and inward states and actions are virtuous. What excellent companions these are in Paradise! And if We had ordered them (saying), "Kill yourselves (i.e. the innnocent ones kill the guilty ones) or leave your homes," very few of them would have done it; but if they had done what they were told, it would have been better for them, and would have strengthened their conviction And indeed We would then have bestowed upon them a great reward from Ourselves And indeed We would have guided them to the straight way And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, then they will be in the company of those on whom Allah has bestowed His grace, of the Prophets, the Siddiqin, the martyrs, and the righteous. In the verses appearing immediately earlier, the promise of a great reward was made to special addressees. at appears in the present verses is a universal promise. that those who obey Allah and His Messenger shall be rewarded as a standing rule. The Salihin or the Righteous are people who restrict themselves, outwardly and inwardly, to doing only what is good and right.

**The love of Thawban and the glad tidings that a person is with those he loves.**

(Whoso obeyeth Allah and the messenger) this verse was revealed about Thawban, the client of Allah's Messenger ﷺ who said: �I am afraid not to meet you in the Hereafter, O Messenger of Allah!� This is because he loved him intensely and could not bear being away from him. Allah's Messenger saw the change in him and so Allah mentioned the honour bestowed on him, saying: whoever obeys Allah regarding the obligations and obeys the Prophet regarding the prophetic practices (they are) in Paradise (with those unto whom Allah hath shown favour, of the Prophets) Muhammad ﷺ and the other prophets, (and the saints) the best among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ (and the martyrs) those who were martyred in the way of Allah (and the righteous) the righteous among the Community of Muhammad ﷺ. Tomorrow, you will be raised with the Prophets, and we will not be able to see you.' The Prophet did not say anything, but later Jibril came down to him with this Ayah,. Greater news than this is in the authentic Hadith collected in the Sahih and Musnad compilations, in Mutawatir form, narrated by several Companions that the Messenger of Allah was asked about the person who loves a people, but his status is not close to theirs. Also there will be yet another form when visits will be made to the strata where they are, as Ibn Jarir has reported on the authority of a narration from Sayyidna Rabi' that the Holy Prophet while explaining this verse, said: 'Those of the strata above will come down to those of the strata below to meet and sit with them.'. It also possible that those of the strata below have the permission to visit and meet those of the higher strata, as the Holy Prophet 4 has, on the basis of this verse, given many people the glad tidings of being with him in the Paradise. According to the Musnad of Ahmad, a man came to the Holy Prophet . and said: 'Ya Rasulallah, I have testified that there is none worthy of worship other than Allah, and that you are the true Messenger of Allah, and I dutifully perform the five prescribed prayers every day, pay the Zakah due on me and fast during the month of Ramadan.' Hearing this, the Holy Prophet said: 'Anyone who dies in this state will be with the prophets, the Siddiqin and the Shuhada - only if he does not disobey his parents.'. This is conclusively proved by what has been reported in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of many uninterrupted chains of narrations from a large body of the noble Companions of the Holy Prophet that he, on being asked as to what will be the status of a person who does belong to a group emotionally but fails to achieve the standards of deeds set by it, said: that is, (on the Day of Resurrection) everyone will be with the ones whom he loves. Whosoever obeys God and the Messenger-they will be with those whom God has blessed: the prophets, the sincerely truthful, the witnesses, and the wholesome. Ibn ʿAbbās says that this verse came down concerning Thawbān, who had become wasted and weak in love for God's Messenger, his back bent and his face yellow. One day the Messenger said to him, "O Thawbān, what is it with you? The hardest sorrow is that in the next world you will be in the highest of the High Chambers, and I will be held back from seeing you.

**Rising above self-interest and convenience to enter Paradise.**

By pursuing a course of selfishness and opportunism in life, the individual incurs the greatest loss, i.e. he fails to find the straight path (as explicitly laid down in the Book of God and sayings of the Prophet) which could have led him to his Lord. One who does not think objectively, who is opportunistic in his thinking, will fail to find that straight path, no matter how clearly it may have been shown to him. This results from his viewing religion, not from a correct perspective, but from the standpoint of his own desires and convenience, so that an image of religion moulded by his own perceptions is formed in his mind. How could such a person be eligible for Paradise, which is to be inhabited only by those who have embraced the Faith, rising above all considerations of self-interest and expediency, who have stood by the covenant of God, being witnesses for the truth to the ultimate extent, and having lead totally pious lives? Until you drown in Remember Me! in the ocean of remembrance, you will not reach the shore of security by the hand of I will remember you [2:152].

"and Allah fully knows ˹who deserves it˺" reassures every sincere lover of Allah and His Prophet—like Thawban in his quiet grief—that Allah alone suffices as the Knower of what lives in the heart, counting every prostration, every act of obedience, and every hidden longing for the righteous, and rewarding each servant in proportion to his sincerity, devotion, and love for the people of truth, while urging every believer to strive with prayer, obedience, and upright character for the ranks of the blessed, before the seventy-first verse turns to the practical command of vigilance and readiness in the path of Allah.
